signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：toolRunner 配合 code_execution_20260120 的核心使用路径完全不可用。两种补救方式均失败——自动传播缺失（硬报错），手动 setMessagesParams 触发无限循环。issue 中明确说明 'There is currently no working path'，属于关键功能完全不可用而非低频边界问题，应为 P0。

source_issues.title: Bug: `toolRunner` does not propagate `container.id` across iterations, and `setMessagesParams` causes duplicate tool call loops
source_issues.evidence: API 报错 'container_id is required when there are pending tool uses generated by code execution with tools'；setMessagesParams 传入 object 时 API 报错 'container: Input should be a valid string'；传入字符串时触发无限工具调用循环，模型反复以相同输入调用 code_execution 和 calculate_sum，无法终止。当前无任何可用路径将客户端 betaTool 与 code_execution_20260120 一起用于流式 toolRunner 循环。

signals.topic: Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.6 模型在 Batch API 中仅调用 1 个工具而非预期的数十个并行工具调用
signals.summary: 在 Message Batches API 中，使用 Opus 4.6 和 Sonnet 4.6 模型时，即使提供 46 个工具定义和足够的 max_tokens（64K-128K）以及 tool_choice='any'，模型仍然仅生成 1 个工具调用即停止；而 Opus 4.5 使用相同请求结构可正确调用 39+ 个工具。这构成 4.6 模型的并行工具调用能力退化，导致大规模数据提取流水线生产级失败。
aliases: Claude 4.6 single tool call batch API
4.6 模型批量 API 并行工具调用退化
Opus 4.6 parallel tool use broken batch
signals.review_reason: 虽为单 issue，但用户影响极为严重：生产医疗平台流水线完全失效，患者数据不完整。issue 中提供了完整的对比测试数据，证明是 4.6 模型的明确退化而非配置问题。虽然可能是后端模型行为而非 SDK 层面可修复的问题，但用户通过 SDK 触发了这一问题，且 issue 在 SDK repo 中提出，SDK 侧可能需要文档澄清或工单路由。因 count=1 且非主流程阻断（流式 API 单独使用不受影响），优先级降为 P1 而非 P0。

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 fail to make parallel tool calls in Batch API
source_issues.evidence: 生产医疗文档处理流水线在切换到 Opus 4.6 后完全失败——原本应调用 46 个工具提取医疗记录，实际仅提取 1 个，患者医疗记录不完整；同一请求结构在 Opus 4.5 下可调用 39+ 工具。作者被迫降级到 Opus 4.5 作为 workaround，放弃了 4.6 的 128K 输出容量和后续模型改进。issue 中包含详细测试矩阵（不同 max_tokens、不同 tool_choice、不同模型对比），stop_reason: 'end_turn'（4.5 正确）vs 'tool_use'（4.6 仅 1 次后停止）。

signals.topic: TextDecoder.decode() 在 Node.js 22 上失败导致 SDK 在 AWS Lambda 无法正常工作
signals.summary: 在 AWS Lambda 环境中使用 Node.js 22 运行时，SDK 抛出错误 'Failed to execute 'decode' on 'TextDecoder': parameter 1 is not of type 'ArrayBuffer'，导致 API 调用完全失败。Node.js 20 可正常工作。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：SDK 在 Node.js 22 主流 LTS 版本上无法工作，直接导致 API 调用失败。虽然是单 issue，但影响 AWS Lambda（常见生产环境）+ Node.js 22（当前主流 LTS）的组合，用户被迫降级到 Node.js 20 作为 workaround，有明确的主流程阻断和用户体验降级证据。count=1 且非 SDK 全量用户受影响，降为 P1。

source_issues.title: TextDecoder.decode() fails on Node.js 22
source_issues.evidence: 在 AWS Lambda + Node.js 22 环境下 SDK 调用失败，报错 'Failed to execute 'decode' on 'TextDecoder': parameter 1 is not of type 'ArrayBuffer'；Workaround 为降级到 Node.js 20；明确是 Node.js 22 的兼容性问题导致主流程阻断。

signals.topic: SDK hangs/deadlocks when string prompts generate high volume of tool calls (~50+) with hooks enabled
signals.summary: Main flow blocking bug: the entire session stalls after ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled. Root cause is the anyio channel fills up and blocks the _read_messages task, preventing the 'result' message that wait_for_result_and_end_input needs. Renders SDK unusable for long-running hooked tool workflows.
aliases: SDK deadlock with high-volume hook tool calls
buffer full deadlock with PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug: the entire session stalls after ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled. Root cause is clearly documented — the anyio channel fills up and blocks the _read_messages task, preventing the 'result' message that wait_for_result_and_end_input needs. High severity blocking issue that renders SDK unusable for long-running hooked tool workflows.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: SDK hangs when string prompt generates more than ~50 tool calls with hooks enabled
source_issues.evidence: Deadlock occurs when internal 100-message buffer fills up; _read_messages blocks on full channel preventing 'result' message from being read; AsyncIterable path avoids this because receive_messages starts immediately

signals.topic: ExitPlanMode terminates SDK turn immediately — plan-then-execute workflows require separate turns
signals.summary: Main flow blocking bug: plan-then-execute pattern is broken in a single turn. After ExitPlanMode, no further tool calls execute — ResultMessage is emitted and receive_messages() completes.
aliases: plan mode exit kills current query
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug: plan-then-execute pattern is broken in a single turn. After ExitPlanMode, no further tool calls execute — ResultMessage is emitted and receive_messages() completes. This breaks orchestrators that rely on plan mode as part of multi-step workflows.

source_issues.title: ExitPlanMode terminates the current SDK turn — no tool execution possible after exiting plan mode
source_issues.evidence: When using ClaudeSDKClient with permission_mode='bypassPermissions', calling ExitPlanMode emits ResultMessage and completes receive_messages() immediately. Tool sequence shows ['EnterPlanMode', 'Read', 'AskUserQuestion', 'ToolSearch', 'ExitPlanMode'] — 'Bash' step never executes.

signals.topic: StructuredOutput tool enters infinite self-correction loop with text output instead of tool calls
signals.summary: The SDK enters an infinite loop where the model outputs StructuredOutput XML text as a TextBlock but never actually calls the tool. This wastes tokens and budget until max budget is hit.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation: the SDK enters an infinite loop where the model outputs StructuredOutput XML text as a TextBlock but never actually calls the tool. The model appears to believe outputting the XML is equivalent to calling the tool. This wastes tokens and budget until max budget is hit — a clear user pain point with repeated failures.

source_issues.title: StructuredOutput gets in a loop
source_issues.evidence: StructuredOutput tool repeatedly emits TextBlock with <StructuredOutput> XML text instead of calling the StructuredOutput tool. It keeps receiving 'Stop hook feedback: You MUST call the StructuredOutput tool' but never actually calls the tool. Runs until max budget is hit.

signals.topic: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes JavaScript renderer crash (H.reduce is not a function)
signals.summary: PostToolUse hook with updatedMCPToolOutput causes renderer crash. Python-side hook works correctly but JavaScript layer crashes. All hooked MCP tools fail simultaneously.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking bug with crash: PostToolUse hook with updatedMCPToolOutput causes renderer crash. Python-side hook works correctly but JavaScript layer crashes. All hooked MCP tools fail simultaneously. Also includes doc/runtime inconsistency for tool_response structure.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes H.reduce is not a function in renderer despite correct hook output
source_issues.evidence: Python hook executes correctly and returns properly shaped content array, but JavaScript renderer crashes with 'H.reduce is not a function'. All three MCP server tools crash simultaneously. Additionally, docs/runtime inconsistency: docs show tool_response as dict with 'content' key but runtime delivers bare list.

signals.topic: bypassPermissions mode skips settings.json shell hooks — only Python callbacks fire
signals.summary: When permission_mode='bypassPermissions', shell hooks configured in ~/.claude/settings.json never fire. Shell hooks are silently ignored, forcing users to rewrite shell hooks as Python callbacks.
signals.review_reason: User-experience degradation: bypassPermissions was expected to skip permission prompts only, not all hooks. Shell hooks in settings.json are silently ignored, forcing users to rewrite shell hooks as Python callbacks. Workaround exists but changes user workflow.

source_issues.title: bypassPermissions mode does not execute settings.json shell hooks
source_issues.evidence: When permission_mode='bypassPermissions', shell hooks configured in ~/.claude/settings.json never fire. PreToolUse hook for AskUserQuestion configured as shell command is never called. Same hook works correctly with 'claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions' directly.

signals.topic: Subprocess spawn failures cause query() to hang or crash with no timeout/error (env missing PATH, Docker, ENOENT)
signals.summary: When the Claude Code CLI subprocess fails to start due to missing environment variables (e.g. PATH wiped by `env: {}`), missing executable, or Docker environment issues, `query()` either hangs forever (no error, no timeout) or exits with code 1. Users have no way to detect or recover from this failure.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct issues (#255, #208, #259) all show the same root cause: SDK subprocess spawn/env failure leads to either indefinite hang (blocking main workflow with no timeout or error signal) or exit code 1 crash. #255 explicitly describes the hang as a blocking issue where even stderr callbacks don't fire. #208 shows this causes restart loops in production. #259 shows Docker environments are also affected. All three represent main flow failure with no recovery path.

source_issues.title: query() hangs forever when CLI subprocess fails to start (ENOENT / missing env)
source_issues.evidence: query() hangs forever when CLI subprocess fails to start. Even adding stderr callback does not surface the error. The readline interface on child stdout pipe blocks forever when child never runs.

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess fails with 'spawn node ENOENT' when PATH not explicitly set in env
source_issues.evidence: SDK subprocess fails to spawn when env option is provided without PATH. Error: 'spawn node ENOENT'. This can trigger infinite restart loops in production systems.

source_issues.title: When calling the SDK in Docker, the following error occurs: 'Claude Code process exited with code 1'
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code process exits with code 1 when running SDK in Docker. Error thrown at getProcessExitError. Debug log shows broken symlink/missing files and No access token for claudeai-mcp.

signals.topic: Race condition in endInput() causes 'write after end' / 'ProcessTransport not ready' errors in production
signals.summary: A race condition in ProcessTransport where endInput() doesn't update state flags causes 'write after end' and 'ProcessTransport not ready for writing' errors when control requests arrive after stdin is ended, especially in single-turn mode with MCP tools.
signals.review_reason: 77+ distinct Sentry errors in 2 weeks is strong evidence of widespread production impact. The race condition is clearly described: endInput() doesn't update state flags while handleControlRequest() runs asynchronously, allowing writes to a closed stream. The error is fatal (ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END). This is a clear main flow failure affecting real users in production on two platforms.

source_issues.title: Race condition: endInput() allows writes to ended stream causing 'write after end' errors
source_issues.evidence: 77+ distinct Sentry issues over 2 weeks affecting users on macOS and Windows. endInput() doesn't set ready=false or mark processStdin as ended, while handleControlRequest() is not awaited — concurrent writes to already-ended stream cause fatal 'ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END' errors in production.

signals.topic: Empty settingSources array causes --setting-sources '' to consume next CLI flag, breaking all default SDK usage
signals.summary: When settingSources is not explicitly provided, the SDK passes --setting-sources '' (empty string) to the Claude Code CLI, which then consumes the next flag (e.g. --permission-mode) as its value, causing an 'Invalid setting source' error. This blocks the default usage path for all SDK users.
aliases: Invalid setting source CLI flag error
signals.review_reason: This bug completely blocks the default SDK usage path — any user calling query() without explicitly setting settingSources encounters an immediate failure. The evidence is clear: the simplest possible SDK call breaks. The root cause (empty array passed as empty string to CLI) is well-identified and the workaround requires non-obvious configuration.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Empty settingSources array causes --setting-sources '' to consume next CLI flag
source_issues.evidence: Any query() call without explicit settingSources fails with 'Error processing --setting-sources: Invalid setting source: --permission-mode'. This blocks all default usage of the SDK — even the simplest possible call fails. Workaround requires explicitly setting settingSources: ['user'].

signals.topic: PreToolUse hook permissionDecision 'deny' generates missing tool_result, causing Anthropic API 400 invalid_request_error
signals.summary: When a PreToolUse hook returns permissionDecision: 'deny', the SDK does not generate a corresponding tool_result block for the denied tool_use, causing the Anthropic API to reject subsequent requests with 'invalid_request_error' because tool_use blocks lack matching tool_result blocks.
signals.review_reason: Using permissionDecision: 'deny' in PreToolUse hooks (a core permission control feature) causes an API 400 error that permanently corrupts the session state. This is a critical failure of the hook system itself — users who rely on deny semantics for security/cost control end up breaking their sessions entirely.

source_issues.title: [BUG] permissionDecision: 'deny' in PreToolUse hook causes missing tool_result, leading to API 400 error
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 'invalid_request_error' with message 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after'. The bug corrupts conversation history state, making the session unusable after any denied tool call.

signals.topic: File checkpointing snapshots not created in SDK mode — rewindFiles() always fails
signals.summary: File history snapshot creation is only triggered inside React/Ink interactive UI code paths and is never called in SDK (non-interactive) mode. Without snapshots, file tracking silently fails and rewindFiles() always returns 'No file checkpoint found for this message' — the feature is completely non-functional in SDK mode.
signals.review_reason: The file checkpointing/rewind feature is completely non-functional in SDK mode — it silently fails with no error message, misleading users into thinking the feature is working when it is not. The enableFileCheckpointing option appears to work (no 'not enabled' error) but produces no usable checkpoints. Users relying on this feature for safety-critical file operations are not protected.

source_issues.title: File checkpointing snapshots not created in SDK (non-interactive) mode
source_issues.evidence: enableFileCheckpointing: true is set but rewindFiles() always returns 'No file checkpoint found for this message' in SDK mode. Root cause: snapshot creation function is only called in React component render logic, never in non-interactive SDK code path. File tracking silently fails without any snapshot to attach backups to.

signals.topic: Hardcoded yanked version in claude-code-base-action breaks all action runs
signals.summary: The main branch of claude-code-base-action hardcodes version 2.1.88, which was yanked due to a source map data leak and a compromised axios dependency. All users of the action immediately get 404 errors on native build download and cannot run the action at all.
aliases: hardcoded yanked version breaks all users
native build 404 due to yanked version
signals.review_reason: All users of the action are completely blocked from running it. The hardcoded yanked version makes the action entirely non-functional for the entire user base. This is a critical main-flow failure with a concrete reproduction link.

source_issues.title: claude-code-base-action@main: v2.1.88 native build download returns 404
source_issues.evidence: All users of anthropics/claude-code-base-action@main cannot run the action — native build download returns 404 for the yanked v2.1.88 version. Three retry attempts all fail. Cited example: https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/actions/runs/23799461443/job/69372967990

signals.topic: Self-hosted runners crash on SDK initialization due to browser environment detection false-positive
signals.summary: On self-hosted runners using Bun, the Anthropic SDK incorrectly detects a browser environment and crashes with 'dangerouslyAllowBrowser' error, making the action unusable on all self-hosted runner deployments up to v1.0.79. Users must pin to v1.0.72 (SDK 0.2.76) and forgo all security/feature updates.
aliases: self-hosted runner SDK crash bun browser detection
signals.review_reason: Action immediately crashes on all self-hosted runner deployments, completely blocking use of the action on self-hosted infrastructure. Users are forced to pin an older version and forgo security updates as the only workaround, representing a sustained block with no clean resolution.

source_issues.title: v1.0.79: SDK crashes with dangerouslyAllowBrowser error on self-hosted runners
source_issues.evidence: All self-hosted runners tested (3 separate runners, Ubuntu 24.04, Bun 1.3.6) crash immediately during SDK initialization with dangerouslyAllowBrowser error. Version regression: v1.0.72 works (SDK 0.2.76), v1.0.79 fails (SDK 0.2.84). Workaround requires pinning to old version, blocking all security/feature updates.

signals.topic: GitHub MCP server Docker container cannot validate TLS certificates on GitHub Enterprise Server with internal CAs
signals.summary: The GitHub MCP server Docker container does not mount the host's CA certificate bundle, causing all API calls to fail with TLS verification errors on GitHub Enterprise Server instances using internal/private CAs. No workaround exists — the action is non-functional for all GHES users with internal certificate authorities, which is the standard enterprise configuration.
aliases: GHES MCP server TLS CA certificate error
MCP server Docker container internal CA trust issue
signals.review_reason: Action is completely non-functional for a broad class of enterprise users (GHES with internal CAs). While only one issue is reported, this is a well-understood infrastructure pattern where the single report represents a systemic gap affecting the entire enterprise segment with no workaround available.

source_issues.title: GitHub MCP server fails on GHES with internal CA certificates — no way to configure TLS trust
source_issues.evidence: All GitHub Enterprise Server deployments using internal CAs (self-signed or corporate) are completely broken — every MCP server API call fails with 'x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'. No input, env var, or Docker argument exists to configure CA trust. This is extremely common in corporate environments. Root cause: Docker command in install-mcp-server.ts has no CA certificate volume mount.

signals.topic: allowed_bots bypasses actor check but not permission check — bot actors (e.g. GitHub Copilot) fail with 404
signals.summary: The allowed_bots input bypasses the human actor check but does not bypass the write permission check. Bot actors like GitHub Copilot (login: 'Copilot') fail with 404 from the collaborators API because they are not repository collaborators, and their login lacks the [bot] suffix. This blocks the Copilot review triage workflow entirely.
aliases: Copilot bot actor permission check failure
signals.review_reason: A key documented use case (Copilot review triage workflow) is completely non-functional. The allowed_bots feature is inconsistently applied — it bypasses one validation but not another, making it unreliable for its documented purpose. The workaround adds significant complexity and latency.

source_issues.title: allowed_bots bypasses actor check but not permission check — bot actors still fail with 404
source_issues.evidence: When GitHub Copilot (actor: 'Copilot', type: Bot) triggers a pull_request_review event with allowed_bots: 'Copilot', the action fails with 'Copilot is not a user' and 404 from the collaborators API. The permission check runs before the actor check and throws before reaching allowed_bots logic. No workaround except re-dispatching via workflow_dispatch with a human actor.

signals.topic: Intensive Claude Code Action PR review loops trigger false-positive account bans on Claude Pro/MAX
signals.summary: When users run intensive PR review loops through the action — where @claude commands cause repeated automated commits and re-reviews from GitHub infrastructure IPs — the safety system misclassifies this as bot-like scripted activity and permanently bans the account. The action provides no rate-limit awareness, causing users to lose access to their accounts even though the usage pattern is entirely within the intended official integration flow.
aliases: account ban false positive from intensive review loops
action-triggered ban on legitimate PR review usage
signals.review_reason: Account-level service denial (permanent ban) from a legitimate, officially-supported workflow is a critical user harm. Even though the issue is closed, the problem pattern (high-frequency automated requests from GitHub infrastructure appearing bot-like) is structural and the 26-comment thread with ongoing activity confirms continued user impact.

source_issues.title: [Possible Bug] False-positive bans when using Claude Code Action for intensive PR review loops
source_issues.evidence: User reproduced this twice on two separate accounts — both were banned shortly after enabling the action and running normal PR review workflows. Third account using identical workflow without the action was not banned. All automated actions originate from GitHub servers/IPs, which the safety system misclassifies as scripted/automated behavior. The issue is closed (2025-11-18) but remains recently active with 26 comments indicating ongoing user impact.

signals.topic: Prompt Cache bug causes 10–20x token inflation, burning through weekly/monthly quotas in minutes
signals.summary: Known Prompt Cache bug causes token consumption to inflate 10–20x above normal. Users report 45% of weekly Pro limit consumed by Tuesday noon, and 20% of 5-hour window consumed in 10 minutes. Users had to drastically simplify projects to stay functional, losing project structure in the process. Some paid for Claude Code to fix its own incorrect output twice.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users both reporting 10-20x token inflation caused by the same Prompt Cache bug (referenced as #38239). Direct monetary impact: Pro plan users burning weekly quotas in hours. One user explicitly links both issues to the same root cause. Count=2 after deduplication.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Prompt Cache causes excessive token consumption (10-20x inflation)
source_issues.evidence: 10-20x token inflation from Prompt Cache bug. One full work day lost, 45% of weekly Pro limit consumed by Tuesday noon. Project had to be drastically simplified. References GitHub Issue #38239 as root cause.

source_issues.title: Dramatic quota consumption increase — 20% in 10 minutes vs full day's work yesterday
source_issues.evidence: 20% of 5-hour quota consumed in first 10 minutes for trivial work (fraction of yesterday's workload). Pays twice: once for Claude's incorrect output, again to fix it. Explicitly links to #38239 cache bug.

signals.topic: Cowork folder picker opens blank, preventing dot folder access and causing infinite retry loops
signals.summary: The request_cowork_directory tool opens a blank macOS folder picker with no pre-populated path. Two consequences: (1) dot folders like ~/.claude are hidden by macOS GUI picker, making them unreachable; (2) user cancellation and inability-to-navigate return identical 'cancelled' responses, causing Claude to retry the same call 4+ times in a loop. Related issue: Claude ignores explicit user corrections in the retry loop.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but causally linked issues: blank folder picker blocks access to Claude's own data directories, and Claude's retry loop ignores user corrections, causing session disruption. The combination means users cannot access key project directories and cannot intervene to break the loop. Count=2 after deduplication.

source_issues.title: [BUG] request_cowork_directory opens blank folder picker instead of prompting for a specific named path
source_issues.evidence: Folder picker opens blank. Dot folders (~/.claude, ~/.config) unreachable via macOS GUI picker. Tool returns identical 'cancelled' for intentional dismiss and cannot-navigate cases, causing 4+ identical failed retries.

source_issues.title: [MODEL] Claude ignores explicit user corrections when stuck in a failing tool retry loop
source_issues.evidence: Claude verbally acknowledges corrections but re-executes the same failing call. Root cause: retry-on-failure path does not re-process conversation for new user instructions before each retry. Loop only broke after significant escalation in user frustration. Explicitly linked to #41657 as trigger.

signals.topic: Yanked release v2.1.88 breaks all session features (skills/MCP/commands), wasting entire work session and tokens
signals.summary: Release v2.1.88 was yanked due to accidental source code leak (59.8MB source map). All slash commands, MCP servers, and custom commands became undetectable. Users wasted entire sessions debugging, then spent additional tokens on downgrade and recovery — zero productive output for the session cost.
signals.review_reason: Single-incident broken release causing complete session failure and direct token cost loss. While count=1 (single issue), the evidence shows P0-level impact: full workflow blockage plus quantifiable monetary loss from tokens spent on both the broken session and the recovery/downgrade process.

source_issues.title: [Bug] v2.1.88 yanked release caused wasted session + significant token loss
source_issues.evidence: Entire session unusable: skills broken, MCP servers invisible, commands not discovered. Additional tokens consumed on diagnosis, downgrade, and recovery. User requests token credit reset.

signals.topic: MCP servers configured with API key headers fail due to incorrect OAuth dynamic client registration
signals.summary: When MCP servers use API key authentication (e.g., Google Stitch, Supabase), Claude Code ignores the provided headers and attempts OAuth dynamic client registration, which these servers don't support. Users get 'Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration' error, making MCP integrations with API key auth completely non-functional.
signals.review_reason: MCP is a key feature; its authentication mechanism is fundamentally broken for API-key-based servers. Users who configure MCP servers per documentation get silent OAuth fallback that fails, making the feature completely non-functional for a documented use case. Count=1 but the pattern affects an entire class of MCP configurations.

source_issues.title: Stitch MCP (stitch.googleapis.com) fails with 'Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration'
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code ignores headers config and attempts OAuth discovery on API-key-authenticated MCP servers. Error: 'Incompatible auth server: does not support dynamic client registration'. Affects Stitch MCP and likely other Google/generic MCP servers using API keys.

signals.topic: GitHub connector regression: OAuth shows 'Connected' but no MCP tools available in session
signals.summary: A regression of #23775 (closed fixed Feb 14, 2026): after completing the GitHub OAuth flow, the connector shows 'Connected' but no GitHub MCP tools are available. Root cause: the OAuth flow only requests 'user:inference' scope and never requests 'user:mcp_servers'. Users cannot perform GitHub operations (list issues, read repos, etc.) despite completing auth.
aliases: GitHub MCP tools unavailable after connect
signals.review_reason: Regression of a previously fixed bug — a key integration feature (GitHub MCP) is completely broken despite UI showing successful connection. The OAuth scope is missing entirely, not a configuration error. Users lose workflow functionality without any error message explaining why. Count=1 but directly related to multiple prior reports (#28695, #26259, #23775).

source_issues.title: [BUG] Cowork GitHub connector shows Connected but exposes no MCP tools — OAuth token missing user:mcp_servers scope (regression of #23775)
source_issues.evidence: Regression of #23775 (fixed Feb 14 2026). Token granted only 'user:inference' scope — 'user:mcp_servers' never requested. Connector shows Connected with no functional tools. Claude incorrectly declares GitHub access impossible, attempts headless browser workarounds. Related open issues: #28695, #26259.

signals.topic: iMessage self-chat silently drops incoming messages due to is_from_me flag corruption from iCloud sync
signals.summary: macOS iCloud sync intermittently marks the owner's incoming self-chat messages as is_from_me=1 instead of is_from_me=0. The plugin unconditionally drops all is_from_me=1 rows, causing user messages to vanish silently with no response from Claude.
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues (#1169 and #1173) both rooted in the same blanket is_from_me=1 filter in iMessage server.ts. Users experience silent, total message loss — text messages and image attachments vanish without any indication. The self-chat use case is a core iMessage plugin scenario (especially for headless/server Claude Code deployments), and the iCloud sync timing issue is not deterministic or user-correctable. Both text and image delivery fail.

source_issues.title: iMessage self-chat: is_from_me=1 on incoming messages breaks delivery
source_issues.evidence: Concrete evidence from chat.db showing user's own messages from iPhone arriving as is_from_me=1 and being dropped. Multiple messages confirmed dropped: 'i don't know for now...', 'hello', 'great so did you commit it yet?' — all silently ignored by Claude.

source_issues.title: imessage: self-chat image attachments silently dropped (is_from_me=1 filter)
source_issues.evidence: Image attachments in self-chat only exist as is_from_me=1 rows (attachment metadata present only on those rows). The blanket is_from_me filter drops all self-chat images before they reach attachment-extraction logic. Chat.db evidence shows image rows only present as is_from_me=1.

signals.topic: Discord and iMessage permission relay breaks after user responds to permission prompt
signals.summary: After a user clicks Allow/Deny on a permission relay prompt in Discord (or iMessage), Claude Code stops sending replies to the channel. The session becomes unresponsive from the user's perspective despite the terminal session being active.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues: Discord permission relay leaves the channel broken after approval (#1174), and iMessage sends permission prompts to the wrong destination (#1185). For Discord, this is a session-breaking failure that makes the channel unusable after any permission event. For iMessage, the permission relay is completely non-functional in headless setups, forcing users to fall back to terminal/Telegram for approvals. Both directly block the multi-channel use case.

source_issues.title: Discord: messages not delivered after permission relay Allow/Deny
source_issues.evidence: Clear repro steps: click Allow/Deny on permission relay in Discord DM, Claude Code processes the tool but no reply is delivered back to Discord. Subsequent messages may also fail. Workarounds require expanding allow list or using external hooks.

source_issues.title: Feature Request: iMessage channel plugin permission relay should support sending to allowlisted sender, not only self-chat
source_issues.evidence: iMessage permission prompts are sent exclusively to self-chat, which remote users on headless/server deployments never see. User must approve via Telegram or terminal — defeating the purpose of multi-channel support. Regression from plugin v0.0.1 which relayed permissions to the requesting sender.

signals.topic: Plugin submission/publishing process lacks transparency and feedback for rejected plugins
signals.summary: Plugin submissions rejected via the dashboard show no feedback or explanation. Users cannot determine why their submission was rejected or what criteria to meet. Confusing gap between 'published' status and actual CLI availability.
signals.review_reason: Two issues (#1186 and #1168) document a confusing submission-to-publication workflow. One issue shows a 'Published' plugin that cannot be installed via CLI (#1187 is the follow-up). The core pain is experience degradation: plugin developers invest effort in submissions only to receive no actionable feedback on rejection, and no clarity on whether their plugin type is even eligible.

source_issues.title: Unclear how to get listed after getting reviewed and published (listed on community plugins but not here)
source_issues.evidence: Plugin shows 'Published' status on claude.ai dashboard but is not present in claude-plugins-official repo and cannot be installed via CLI. User explicitly requests better documentation about publishing timelines and processes.

source_issues.title: Submission rejected with no feedback — how to meet acceptance criteria?
source_issues.evidence: Plugin rejected with no explanation. User resubmitted with improvements but has no way to know what was wrong with the first submission. Also questions whether skills-only plugins are even eligible for this directory.

signals.topic: Telegram plugin spawns two polling processes causing ~50% of inbound messages to be silently lost
signals.summary: Single Claude Code session loads .mcp.json from both cached and marketplace source directories, spawning two competing Telegram polling processes. Since Telegram delivers each update to only one consumer, ~50% of messages are randomly dropped with no user notification.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker: the Telegram channel is the primary communication path and approximately half of all inbound messages are silently dropped. The issue has clear root cause evidence, reproducible steps, and no automatic resolution — every session启动 suffers the same failure. This directly defeats the core purpose of the Telegram plugin integration.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: single session spawns two polling processes (marketplace + cache .mcp.json both loaded)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed root cause: both cache and marketplace .mcp.json files are loaded in one session, spawning two bun processes. Telegram getUpdates delivers each message to one consumer randomly. ~50% message loss in active use. Workaround requires manually disabling marketplace .mcp.json.

signals.topic: iMessage plugin sends permission prompts to unintended recipients due to incorrect SELF address detection
signals.summary: The SELF address detection includes non-self addresses from chat.last_addressed_handle, causing permission request messages (containing tool descriptions and parameters) to be sent to unintended iMessage recipients such as partners' phone numbers.
signals.review_reason: This is a privacy/security concern with clear user impact: permission prompts containing sensitive tool descriptions and parameters are being sent to unintended third parties. The root cause is well-documented with SQL evidence. While only affecting multi-user Mac setups, the information leak is non-trivial — tool parameters can include file paths, API keys in tool calls, and business-specific prompts.

source_issues.title: iMessage: SELF detection picks up non-self addresses from chat.last_addressed_handle
source_issues.evidence: SQL evidence showing last_addressed_handle contains other people's phone numbers alongside user's own. Permission prompts (🔐 Permission request [code]...) include tool descriptions and parameters, which are sent to these unintended recipients. Demonstrated with real phone numbers in the issue.

signals.topic: MCP Playwright 课程实操说明缺少关键步骤，导致用户遭遇静默失败
signals.summary: Claude Code in Action 课程中 Playwright MCP 的安装说明不完整，用户执行 `claude mcp add playwright` 后 MCP 工具不会正常出现（静默失败），缺少安装浏览器、执行系统依赖安装脚本、重启 Claude Code 三个必要步骤；Ubuntu 25.x 还存在包名不兼容的额外问题。
aliases: MCP server silent failure due to missing setup steps
signals.review_reason: 该问题有明确用户影响：课程实操环节因说明缺失而完全阻断，用户遭遇静默失败（MCP 工具从不出现），且 Ubuntu 25.x 包名不兼容进一步加剧问题。虽然 count=1、仅单仓，但属于课程主流程阻断，且有具体技术证据支撑，标记为 P1。排除项 #144 为纯测试/空 body，不纳入分析。

source_issues.title: Claude Code in Action: MCP Playwright setup instructions missing critical steps
source_issues.evidence: 用户在按课程步骤配置 Playwright MCP 时遭遇静默失败——MCP 工具从不出现，导致实操环节完全无法推进。课程说明仅给出 `claude mcp add playwright` 命令，缺少安装浏览器 (`npx playwright install`)、安装系统依赖 (`sudo npx playwright install-deps`) 和重启 Claude Code 三个关键步骤；Ubuntu 25.x 还需额外手动安装包。

signals.topic: docx skill generates Word documents that trigger repair dialog on open
signals.summary: The docx skill's docx-js pipeline emits malformed XML (incorrect footnote separators, missing required document parts like endnotes.xml and webSettings.xml, missing w:space attributes on borders, missing w:tblLook on tables) that causes Microsoft Word to show a repair dialog every time the generated .docx is opened. While Word successfully repairs with no content loss, the dialog erodes trust when sharing documents with non-technical collaborators and creates friction in document workflows.
aliases: docx XML malformation causes Word repair dialog
Word prompts to repair docx skill generated documents
signals.review_reason: Real user pain point confirmed by issue #570. The docx skill generates .docx files that fail to open cleanly in Microsoft Word — a primary target application — triggering a repair dialog on every open. While no content is lost, this is a recurring workflow friction that erodes trust, especially when non-technical collaborators receive these files. The evidence includes detailed XML diff analysis showing exact root causes (4 distinct structural XML issues), affecting any user who generates Word documents via the docx skill and opens them in Word. This is a quality/defect issue, not a feature request or roadmap discussion.

source_issues.title: docx skill: footnote separators and table XML patterns trigger Word repair dialog
source_issues.evidence: Documents generated using the docx skill's docx-js pipeline open in Microsoft Word with a repair dialog. Word successfully repairs them with no content loss, but the dialog erodes trust when sharing documents with non-technical collaborators. Root causes identified via XML diff: (1) footnote separator/continuation footnotes include w:footnoteRef/w:rStyle that only belong in content footnotes; (2) missing required word/endnotes.xml and word/webSettings.xml; (3) missing w:space on border definitions; (4) missing w:tblLook on tables.

signals.topic: algorithmic-art skill template missing action buttons breaks expected functionality
signals.summary: The algorithmic-art skill expects Regenerate, Reset, and Download PNG actions, but the viewer.html template only exposes the Reset button. This mismatch means users of the skill see missing or non-functional action buttons, breaking the documented skill experience.
aliases: viewer.html missing Regenerate and Download PNG buttons
signals.review_reason: Template-code mismatch means skill-documented functionality (Regenerate and Download PNG) is unavailable to users. However, only 1 issue reported, it is a non-blocking UX degradation rather than main-process failure, and no other affected repos are involved. Downgraded to P2 per priority rules.

source_issues.title: Align algorithmic-art viewer actions with skill requirements
source_issues.evidence: The viewer template has only Reset in the Actions section, but the skill expects Regenerate, Reset, and Download PNG. Users of the algorithmic-art skill will encounter missing action buttons (Regenerate, Download PNG) that the skill promises but the template does not render.

signals.topic: MCP extension processes not cleaned up on session end, causing memory leak
signals.summary: When Goose sessions end (terminal close, crash, unclean shutdown), spawned MCP extension processes (Slack, Google Drive, Snowflake, etc.) remain orphaned as zombie processes consuming memory indefinitely, leading to resource exhaustion over time.
aliases: MCP server not terminated on session end
signals.review_reason: Memory leak causing resource exhaustion (187→9 processes, 2.8GB→58MB). Over time, accumulating orphaned MCP processes consume GBs of RAM until the system becomes unresponsive or OOM — this is a de-facto main-flow blocker for long-running sessions. Issue provides quantitative evidence (before/after metrics) and identifies an existing but unwired fix (PR #7411 SessionEnd hooks).

source_issues.title: MCP extension processes are not cleaned up when Goose sessions end, causing memory leak
source_issues.evidence: Real-world metric: 187 Python processes, ~2,864 MB RAM consumed before cleanup vs 9 processes, ~58 MB after cleanup. 356 stale MCP processes (~3.9 GB). SessionEnd lifecycle hooks exist (PR #7411) but not wired for MCP cleanup.

signals.topic: Goose CLI segfaults (SIGSEGV/EXC_BAD_ACCESS) during tool execution/approval on macOS
signals.summary: Goose CLI crashes with segfault when user approves tool execution (Playwright, Fetch) on macOS, leaving the server alive but making the CLI unusable.
aliases: CLI crash on tool call approval
signals.review_reason: Hard crash (SIGSEGV) during tool execution/approval — a core workflow step. macOS crash report confirms EXC_BAD_ACCESS. Reproducible by multiple extensions (Playwright, Fetch), indicating a systemic CLI stability issue rather than an edge case. User's main task is completely blocked.

source_issues.title: segfault during tool execution/approval
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced on macOS with both Fetch and Playwright extensions. Crash report shows EXC_BAD_ACCESS/SIGSEGV/KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS. Tool execution/approval is a core workflow step — crash here blocks the entire task from completing.

signals.topic: zhipu provider hardcoded base URL prevents GLM-5.1 access for Coding Plan subscribers
signals.summary: The built-in zhipu provider hardcodes the standard API endpoint, but GLM-5.1 and other Coding Plan models are only accessible via the separate Coding Plan endpoint, causing permission error 1220 for valid subscribers.
aliases: Coding Plan models inaccessible via built-in zhipu provider
signals.review_reason: Key feature (GLM-5.1 model access) completely unusable for Coding Plan subscribers due to hardcoded URL mismatch. Multiple workarounds all fail. Direct evidence: same API key works via curl but not via Goose. Not P0 because count=1 and it's a specific provider/model issue rather than broad main-flow block.

source_issues.title: Built-in zhipu provider: hardcoded base URL prevents Coding Plan GLM-5.1 access
source_issues.evidence: Error 1220 returned for GLM-5.1 even with active GLM Coding Plan (Max tier). Same API key works via curl against the Coding Plan endpoint. All workarounds fail: custom provider takes precedence, OPENAI_BASE_URL causes 401, ZHIPU_BASE_URL is ignored by built-in provider.

signals.topic: Agent loop lacks automatic retry for transient provider errors, causing mid-task failures with no recovery
signals.summary: The agent loop breaks immediately on transient errors (network drops, stream decode errors, rate limits, server errors) instead of retrying, causing long-running tasks to fail mid-execution with no user-configurable recovery.
signals.review_reason: Long-running tasks fail mid-execution due to lack of retry for recoverable errors (network glitch, rate limit, stream decode). Real user impact: 4m25s of progress lost on a single transient error. Not P0 because count=1, but clearly significant UX degradation for users running multi-minute tasks.

source_issues.title: feat: automatic retry for transient provider errors in agent loop
source_issues.evidence: Agent loop always breaks on NetworkError, RateLimitExceeded, ServerError, and 'Stream decode error' RequestFailed. Real error message shown: 'Request failed: Stream decode error: error decoding response body. Please retry if you think this is a transient or recoverable error.' with 4m25s elapsed time lost.

signals.topic: User messages sent mid-tool-execution are silently queued with no acknowledgement, causing message loss perception and duplicate sends
signals.summary: When Goose is executing a tool, user-typed messages are silently queued without visual acknowledgement, leading users to believe messages were lost and send duplicates, resulting in confusing multi-message bursts after the tool completes.
aliases: user message lost perception during tool execution
signals.review_reason: UX confusion during tool execution: no acknowledgement for queued messages leads to duplicate sends and message bursts. Not blocking (user can wait for tool to finish) but creates a confusing experience and wasted effort. P2 due to count=1 and non-blocking nature.

source_issues.title: bug: user messages sent mid-task are delayed / not picked up until current tool completes
source_issues.evidence: User messages during long tool execution (10+ seconds) get silently queued with no visual feedback. Users send follow-up messages believing the first was lost, resulting in a burst of messages processed after the tool finishes. Affects both Desktop and CLI.

signals.topic: Docker 部署中 Gateway 和 LangGraph 容器之间文件隔离，上传文件对 AI 不可见
signals.summary: Docker compose 部署时 Gateway 容器和 LangGraph 容器未共享 uploads 目录，导致前端上传的图片在 Gateway 容器存在但 LangGraph 容器为空，AI 无法读取图片。同时自定义技能 (custom skills) 在 Docker 环境下也无法被 DeerFlow 访问，提示用户需从本地终端运行。
aliases: custom skills not accessible in Docker
signals.review_reason: Docker 容器文件隔离问题导致两个关键功能受损：图片上传后 AI 完全无法读取（阻断主流程），自定义技能在 Docker 环境下不可用。4 个 issue 均指向容器间文件系统未正确共享或挂载，证据明确（Gateway 容器有文件但 LangGraph 容器为空）。

source_issues.title: 图片上传后 LangGraph 容器看不到文件，Gateway 和 LangGraph 容器 uploads 目录未同步
source_issues.evidence: 前端上传图片后 Gateway 容器的 uploads 目录有文件，但 LangGraph 容器的 uploads 目录为空，AI 无法读取图片。API 接口返回文件已上传成功，但 LangGraph 容器不可见。

source_issues.title: ###custom skills -- running error in Docker environment (~/skills/custom/*)
source_issues.evidence: 自定义技能在本地终端可正常访问，但通过 localhost 或飞书调用时，Docker 环境下的 DeerFlow 无法访问 custom skills，提示用户需从本地终端运行。

source_issues.title: 环境问题
source_issues.evidence: Windows WSL 环境下工具集中缺少代码执行能力（无法运行 python3 或 bash），工具路径访问受限。

source_issues.title: Windows 环境下是否支持本地开发方式？
source_issues.evidence: Windows 本地开发无法启动：check 命令 pnpm 找不到文件（subprocess filenotfounderror），make dev 启动失败（Error 49）。

signals.topic: LLM API 重试阻塞整个 Gateway 事件循环导致服务完全不可用（504），必须重启容器
signals.summary: 当 MiniMax 等 LLM API 偶发超时或网络波动时，内置重试机制触发，每次重试等待 300s 读超时，同步阻塞 asyncio 事件循环，导致所有并发 API 请求返回 504 Gateway Timeout，前端完全无法操作，必须 docker restart。根因包括 PatchedChatMiniMax 超时 300s 过长、ClaudeChatModel 同步路径 time.sleep() 阻塞、CodexChatModel 全同步实现最坏阻塞 906s。
aliases: asyncio event loop blocking on LLM retry
signals.review_reason: 这是生产级阻断问题：单次 LLM 超时重试可导致整个 Gateway 服务完全不可用（504），所有并发用户均受影响，必须重启容器才能恢复。Issue #1684 提供了详细代码证据（根因文件、行号、阻塞时间计算），P0 优先级清晰。Issue #1681 进一步证明 LLM 异常处理不当导致会话锁死，双重证据指向同一个系统设计缺陷。

source_issues.title: BUG-001: LLM API 重试导致整个 Gateway 阻塞（504）
source_issues.evidence: 重试日志显示每次重试间隔 0.4-0.8s，但等待读超时 300s，导致 Gateway 完全无响应，curl localhost:2026/api/threads 返回 504 Gateway Time-out，必须 docker restart 恢复。提供了详细根因分析（代码行号、阻塞时间计算）。

source_issues.title: [runtime] 未正确处理LLM调用异常（如服务器繁忙、超出限额等）
source_issues.evidence: 第三方 LLM 被拒绝后出现 'An internal error occurred'，会话锁死无法继续，即便第三方服务器恢复后也无法使用。堆栈显示 openai.APIError: 当前服务集群负载较高。关联 #1662 和 #1391。

signals.topic: LLM API 调用异常（服务繁忙/超限）未正确处理，会话锁死无法恢复
signals.summary: 第三方 LLM 接口因繁忙、欠费或超限被拒绝时，没有有效的重试、提醒机制。出现 'An internal error occurred' 后会话无法继续，即便第三方服务恢复正常也无法使用，必须新建会话。
aliases: no retry on LLM API errors
signals.review_reason: LLM 异常导致会话完全锁死是严重体验问题：用户反复遇到 'An internal error occurred' 后无法继续对话，即便底层服务恢复也无法使用，必须新建会话重新开始。对于付费 API 用户（欠费/超限场景），经济损失直接叠加在体验损失之上。Issue #1662 和 #1681 均独立复现此问题。

source_issues.title: [runtime] 未正确处理LLM调用异常（如服务器繁忙、超出限额等）
source_issues.evidence: 第三方 LLM 拒绝访问后前端显示 'An internal error occurred'，会话锁死无法继续。日志显示 openai.APIError: 当前服务集群负载较高。第三方服务器恢复正常后会话仍无法使用。

source_issues.title: 用火山引擎coding plan 配置后 老是提示internal error occurred
source_issues.evidence: 配置火山引擎 doubao-seed-2.0-pro 后服务不稳定，频繁出现 internal error occurred，偶尔才能正常回答。

signals.topic: Thinking 模式配置不兼容：界面无法禁用 thinking 且 'minimal' 值与 LiteLLM 不匹配
signals.summary: 用户无法通过界面切换到禁用思考模式，when_thinking_disabled 配置项缺失。当使用 LiteLLM 模型将 thinking 模式切换到 minimal 时，接口报错 'Input should be low, medium or high'，因 DeerFlow 将 'minimal' 透传给 LiteLLM，但 LiteLLM 只支持 low/medium/high。
signals.review_reason: Thinking 模式配置问题影响想禁用思考或使用特定模式的用户。虽然不阻断基本对话，但会导致模型调用 400 错误（minimal 不兼容）以及关键配置项缺失，影响有定制需求的用户。当前 count=2 且均为单一仓库，默认 P2。

source_issues.title: Unable to switch to disabled-thinking mode via the interface, and the 'when_thinking_disabled' configuration is missing
source_issues.evidence: 界面无法切换到禁用思考模式，when_thinking_disabled 配置项缺失。

source_issues.title: thinking mode is switched to minimal failed When use LiteLLM model
source_issues.evidence: LiteLLM 1.82.4 的 reasoning_effort 参数只支持 'low'/'medium'/'high'，DeerFlow 传递 'minimal' 导致 BadRequestError: validation error，reasoning_effort input 'minimal' 不被接受。

signals.topic: Agent 忽略用户上传的文件，优先触发 deep-research 联网搜索而非基于附件内容回答
signals.summary: 当用户上传附件并提出可从文件内容回答的问题时，Agent 绕过文件直接触发 deep-research 联网搜索。根因是 deep-research 技能触发条件过宽（覆盖几乎所有知识型提问），且 UploadsMiddleware 仅注入文件元数据而非内容，导致 Agent 仅凭文件名判断相关性后跳过文件。
aliases: deep-research triggered instead of reading file
signals.review_reason: Agent 忽略用户上传文件直接联网搜索是核心功能异常：用户上传文件的意图被完全忽略，deep-research 技能的宽泛触发条件导致 Agent 决策优先级颠倒（联网优先于本地文件）。Issue #1647 有 6 条评论（最高），Issue #1664 有 3 条评论，说明社区对此问题关注度高。

source_issues.title: [Bug/Feature] Agent 忽略已上传的文件，直接触发 deep-research 联网搜索，而非优先基于文件内容回答
source_issues.evidence: 用户上传附件后 Agent 仅凭文件名判断'可能不相关'就跳过，从未调用 read_file。deep-research 技能描述覆盖所有知识型提问（'what is X', 'explain X'），优先级高于本地文件。即使 Agent 读取了文件，仍倾向判断'信息不足'并触发 deep-research。

source_issues.title: 结果奇奇怪怪，不遵循skill
source_issues.evidence: 自定义技能要求 Agent 用特定方式查询数据，但 Agent 写了脚本后直接从网络获取数据，完全不遵循技能指令。同一模型配置下 nanobat 和 copaw 自定义技能无此问题。

signals.topic: Cline Kanban feature failures: session crash recovery, board task creation, and LiteLLM model access
signals.summary: Multiple distinct failures in Cline Kanban: sessions are lost and not recovered after process crash (#10052), Kanban board does not create tasks (#10053), LiteLLM model access fails with HTTP 500 (#10046), and diff panel shows 'No working changes' for tasks with actual diffs (#10042).
signals.review_reason: Kanban feature has four distinct failure modes covering core functionality: crash recovery (cards lost and unrecoverable), task creation not reflected on board, LiteLLM incompatibility, and broken diff visualization. All four impair the Kanban workflow significantly.

source_issues.title: cline kanban: not restoring sessions after process crash
source_issues.evidence: WSL crashed (likely OOM). After restart, cards were in trash. Restore takes very long and some never restore. Cards stuck 'in progress' but nothing progresses.

source_issues.title: Cline Kanban not using kanban board, no tasks created and no orchestration on board, but execution in chat window
source_issues.evidence: AI model executed request but created no project or tasks on the Kanban board. All work done in chat window only; Kanban board remained empty.

source_issues.title: Cline Kanban cannot access model name from LiteLLM (but working properly in cline TUI and cline VScode ext)
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 500 error from LiteLLM when using Cline Kanban. Same model works correctly in Cline TUI and VSCode extension. Kanban-specific compatibility issue.

source_issues.title: Kanban view shows 'No working changes' for tasks that have diffs
source_issues.evidence: Tasks with actual file modifications show 'No working changes' in the Kanban view diff panel. Diff viewer fails to display changes even when files were modified.

signals.topic: Terminal/bash command execution failures causing hangs, missing results, or syntax errors
signals.summary: Multiple independent issues all result in terminal command execution failures: heredoc commands hang with missing results (#10066), HTML-entity-escaped operators cause syntax errors (#10064), and bash syntax errors with escaped quotes/parentheses stall the terminal (#10063). All three block the core tool execution workflow.
signals.review_reason: Three independent issues, all causing core tool execution to fail or hang. Issue #10066 is particularly severe because Cancel also freezes the UI (double-blocking). Issue #10064 demonstrates a complete failure of the execute_command tool due to HTML entity double-encoding. All three verified with reproduction steps and confirmed to work correctly outside Cline, isolating the root cause to Cline's terminal integration layer.

source_issues.title: Heredoc execution breaks terminal output handling (`result missing`/hang), and Cancel may freeze chat UI
source_issues.evidence: Heredoc commands executed through Cline hang or return 'result missing'. Cancel button turns grey and Resume becomes unavailable. Control check outside Cline confirms same commands work in regular terminal.

source_issues.title: execute_command renders && literally in bash command, causing `syntax error near unexpected token ';&'` and stuck process
source_issues.evidence: AI emits execute_command with HTML-escaped && as &&, causing bash syntax error. Process then gets stuck.

source_issues.title: Terminal stalls after bash syntax error when command contains escaped quotes/parentheses
source_issues.evidence: Commands with escaped quotes/parentheses trigger bash parse error, then terminal hangs indefinitely instead of returning non-zero exit + error output.

signals.topic: CLI mode switching breaks write_to_file tool availability (Plan/Act mode)
signals.summary: Switching from Plan to Act mode via keyboard shortcut (or -p parameter) causes write_to_file tool to become unavailable or unresponsive, even though the UI shows Act mode. Mode state and UI state fall out of sync.
signals.review_reason: Two reports (one closed as duplicate) showing mode switching desynchronizes UI state from actual system state, rendering write_to_file completely unusable. This is a core file editing workflow blocker in the CLI.

source_issues.title: ACT MODE (Tab)工具不可用问题 / ACT MODE (Tab) Tools Unavailable Issue
source_issues.evidence: After mode switch, UI shows 'Act (Tab)' but environment details show 'Current Mode: PLAN MODE'. write_to_file tool returns error 'not available in PLAN MODE'. Cannot switch modes.

source_issues.title: [Bug] write_to_file tool becomes unresponsive after switching from Plan to Act mode via shortcut
source_issues.evidence: After mode switching via keyboard shortcut, write_to_file stops working. Restart temporarily fixes but issue recurs on next mode switch. Issue closed as duplicate of #10041.

signals.topic: JetBrains plugin multi-file edit approval buttons disabled after first file
signals.summary: When Cline proposes changes to multiple files in a single request on the JetBrains plugin, the Save and Reject buttons become disabled (greyed out) starting from the second file, preventing users from completing multi-file edit approvals.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the multi-file edit approval flow on JetBrains. Users must work around by submitting one file at a time, which significantly degrades the core editing workflow.

source_issues.title: Save/Reject buttons become disabled on second file during multi-file edit approval
source_issues.evidence: First file: buttons work. Second file onwards: buttons disabled and cannot be clicked. Workaround requires editing one file per request, severely limiting workflow efficiency.

signals.topic: CLI light theme visibility is very poor with no theme customization options

signals.topic: R2 存储挂载反复失败，导致备份与配置同步功能不可用
signals.summary: 多个用户遭遇 R2 bucket 挂载失败，Backup Now 按钮报 "Config sync failed" 或 S3FS 错误。该问题由进程状态轮询逻辑未正确处理 'starting' 状态导致挂载检查提前退出，引起 R2 持久化存储不可用。
signals.review_reason: count=3 且达到阈值；三项 issue 均指向同一根因（R2 挂载流程 bug），覆盖核心备份持久化功能；用户直接体验为 Backup Now 按钮无法使用、配置无法保存，均为关键功能阻断。

source_issues.title: Can't mount R2
source_issues.evidence: 用户按文档完整配置后点击 Backup Now 仍报 'Config sync failed'，YouTube 评论区多位用户反馈卡在此步骤。R2 挂载是核心备份/持久化功能，该失败直接导致数据无法落盘。

source_issues.title: waitForProcess and isR2Mounted don't account for 'starting' process status
source_issues.evidence: 根本原因：轮询循环只检查 'running' 状态，'starting' 阶段即退出，导致 R2 挂载检查误判为失败。补丁已验证修复了 Backup Now 间歇性失败的问题。

source_issues.title: cannot mount R2: S3FS mount failed: multiple entries for same bucket in passwd file
source_issues.evidence: R2 挂载报 S3FS 错误，删除容器后问题仍然存在，说明是挂载流程本身的 bug，导致 R2 持久化存储不可用。

signals.topic: 容器未在请求处理前启动，导致所有请求均返回 500 错误
signals.summary: sandbox.start() 调用缺失，容器在未启动状态下即处理请求，导致每次请求都失败并报 'The container is not running' 错误。同时网关在特定版本下冷启动后立即崩溃，令主流程完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: 两项 issue 均为主流程阻断性 bug；#291 影响所有请求（100% 阻断率），#179 影响特定版本所有用户；虽然 count=2 未达 P0 阈值，但两处均为冷启动/容器就绪类缺陷，用户影响明确且严重。

source_issues.title: Container not started before containerFetch: missing sandbox.start() call
source_issues.evidence: 明确复现路径：部署后任意请求均触发 'The container is not running' 错误并返回 500，网关日志可见该错误。根因是 src/index.ts 中 getSandbox() 后未调用 await sandbox.start()，导致容器未 boot 即处理请求。

source_issues.title: Gateway returns HTTP 500 errors and crashes immediately after startup
source_issues.evidence: 网关启动成功、端口可达，但第一个 HTTP 请求即返回 500，随后报 'container is not listening' 并 crash，每次重启均复现。影响该版本（2026.1.24-3）所有用户的主流程。

source_issues.title: Config changes don't persist - dmPolicy keeps reverting to 'pairing'
source_issues.evidence: 用户修改 dmPolicy 配置后，配置会自动回退至 'pairing' 值，配置持久化机制失效，用户设置无法保留。

source_issues.title: TUI Raw Config Saves Don't Save to R2
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 TUI 的 Raw Config 界面填写配置并点击保存后，R2 中的文件内容未更新，需手动直接编辑 R2 文件才能生效。核心配置功能失效。

signals.topic: Sandbox DO 内部 Alarm 阻止容器进入休眠，SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER 配置失效导致成本失控
signals.summary: 用户配置了 SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER=10m 期盼容器空闲后休眠以节省成本，但 Sandbox Durable Object 每 3 分钟产生一次 Alarm，导致容器始终保持活跃，预期 ~$5-10/月实际可能达到 ~$30/月，成本管理机制完全失效。
signals.review_reason: 单条 issue 但用户影响严重：成本管理核心功能（SLEEP_AFTER）完全失效，造成用户直接财务损失（~$30 vs ~$5-10/月）。明确的计费异常证据，故提升为 P1 而非 P2。

source_issues.title: Sandbox container does not sleep with SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER=10m due to recurring Sandbox DO alarms
source_issues.evidence: 用户配置 SANDBOX_SLEEP_AFTER=10m，wrangler tail 显示每 3 分钟出现一次 Sandbox DO Alarm，导致容器始终 warm 而非 sleep。预期省成本特性完全失效，用户承受隐性超额费用。

signals.topic: Cloudchamber 容器挂起导致定时任务/CRON 无法触发

signals.review_reason: 单仓单 issue，但描述清晰：CRON 任务被跳过是用户可感知的自动化功能损失，属于关键功能不可用场景，故保留为 P2。

source_issues.title: Scheduled tasks / cron jobs don't fire in Cloudchamber containers

signals.topic: TextFile input to crews requires vision-capable model despite being text-only content, blocking main workflow
signals.summary: Passing text files via input_files parameter causes ValueError on non-vision models. Users expect text files to be processed as text content, but the system treats them as multimodal input. This is a regression from 1.10 to 1.12.2.
aliases: text file input requires vision model
signals.review_reason: User workflow blocking: passing text files to crews via input_files parameter is a core use case that fails completely with a ValueError, forcing users to use workarounds. This is a documented API regression that breaks expected functionality and forces non-obvious workarounds.

source_issues.title: [BUG] / [HELP] Model does not support multimodal input [...] Use a vision-capable model for TextFile input
source_issues.evidence: Passing TextFiles via input_files parameter results in ValueError on non-vision models. Users expect text files to be processed as text content. This is a regression from crewai 1.10 to 1.12.2. Workaround exists (attaching files directly to tasks) but breaks expected API behavior.

signals.topic: Shared LLM stop words mutation causes cross-agent state pollution in multi-agent crews
signals.summary: When multiple agents share the same LLM instance, each agent's __init__ mutates the shared LLM's stop attribute, causing stop words to accumulate across agents. Agent A's stop words leak into Agent B, causing premature generation termination with no error raised.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation: shared LLM instances cause silent behavioral corruption where agents terminate prematurely due to accumulated stop words from other agents. No error is raised — outputs are subtly wrong. This is a common setup (2+ agents sharing an LLM) that produces wrong results without any indication of failure, making it extremely hard to diagnose.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Shared LLM stop words mutation causes cross-agent state pollution
source_issues.evidence: Multiple agents sharing an LLM instance accumulate stop words across agents. Agent A's stop words leak into Agent B, causing premature generation termination. Silent behavioral degradation with no error raised. Affects all crews with 2+ agents sharing an LLM (common/default case). Code comment acknowledges: 'This may be mutating the shared llm object and needs further evaluation.'

signals.topic: result_as_answer=true ignores tool failure, treating error outputs as final answers
signals.summary: When result_as_answer=True is set, the agent ignores tool success/failure status and uses the tool output (including errors) as the final answer. Tool errors become the agent's final answer without any reflection.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow corruption: when result_as_answer=True is enabled (a documented feature), tool errors are treated as successful outputs and become the agent's final answer without reflection. This causes agents to silently report errors as valid results, breaking the reliability of tool-using workflows. Users cannot distinguish between a successful tool execution and a failed one when this flag is set.

source_issues.title: [BUG] If result_as_answer=true is set, then irrespective of tool's failure or success, tool output which essentially is error returned will become final answer of agent
source_issues.evidence: When result_as_answer=True is set, the agent ignores tool success/failure status and uses the tool output (including errors) as the final answer. This removes the agent's ability to reflect on failed tool executions, causing agents to report errors as valid results.

signals.topic: KeyError crash in LLM response handling when messages key is missing
signals.summary: In LLM response handling, code raises a helpful ValueError for missing messages but then immediately causes a confusing KeyError at a different line, providing inconsistent and misleading error messages.
aliases: confusing error message KeyError vs ValueError
signals.review_reason: Developer experience issue: the code has inconsistent error handling — it raises a helpful ValueError for missing messages but then crashes with a confusing KeyError at a different line. This misleads developers trying to debug LLM response issues. Low frequency (count=1) but the misleading error messages significantly slow down debugging.

source_issues.title: [BUG] KeyError when params missing 'messages' key in _handle_non_streaming_response
source_issues.evidence: In crewai/llm.py, both _handle_non_streaming_response() and _ahandle_non_streaming_response() access params['messages'] directly after already extracting via params.get('messages', []). If messages key is missing, a helpful ValueError is raised at one line but then a confusing KeyError is raised at another line, providing inconsistent error signals.

signals.topic: CLI unusable on Windows when using plan mode with auto model selection

aliases: CLI unusable on Windows with API key
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues both report CLI being completely unusable on Windows in plan mode. #24365 shows a concrete ENOENT error for the sandbox executable, blocking the core workflow. #24327 corroborates the pattern with multiple users affected (screenshot of user complaints) and explicitly confirms it occurs on Windows with plan mode/auto model. This is not a cosmetic issue — the CLI fails to function at all for affected users.

source_issues.title: I can't work with Gemini because a major error occurs: "GeminiSandbox.exe ENOENT"

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI unusable even with API key

signals.topic: TUI hangs indefinitely when API returns 403/auth error for restricted Google accounts

The spinner runs forever with no timeout or exception, blocking the main workflow and forcing manual process kill.
aliases: TUI infinite hang on auth failure
TUI spinner never resolves on API rejection
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker. The CLI's TUI enters an infinite loading loop on restricted accounts instead of displaying a clear error, forcing manual process kill. The user provided exhaustive debugging evidence (direct API calls succeed at 39ms, proving the issue is in CLI error-handling, not network). This affects any user whose Google account triggers API-level restrictions.

source_issues.title: CRITICAL: CLI hangs infinitely in TUI instead of throwing 403/Auth error for restricted Google accounts
source_issues.evidence: User reports TUI goes into infinite loading loop (10+ minutes) on restricted account. Detailed debugging confirms network is fine (direct curl returns 403 instantly). Root cause: CLI fetch wrapper fails to resolve Promise on account-level block, leaving spinner running forever.

signals.topic: Node.js process crashes with heap out of memory during long conversations

signals.review_reason: Process crash causing complete session data loss is a clear P0. The user provided a complete Node.js crash stack trace (heap limit exhaustion during Mark-Compact), and explicitly notes this has happened multiple times, confirming it is a recurring failure rather than a one-off. Main flow is blocked and work is destroyed.

source_issues.title: Node Crashes During Long Conversations
source_issues.evidence: Full Node.js heap crash trace provided. Mark-Compact GC runs repeatedly, reaching heap limit, then FATAL ERROR. Session ID and client info captured. User notes this has happened multiple times.

signals.topic: Paid tier model requests silently routed to inferior model by backend
signals.summary: When users explicitly select gemini-3.1-pro-preview (a premium paid model), the backend silently delegates all requests to gemini-2.5-pro instead. Users pay for Code Assist in Google One AI Pro expecting gemini-3.1-pro-preview capabilities but receive degraded output quality and slower responses.
aliases: Model routing mismatch for paying customers
signals.review_reason: This is a direct cost loss issue for paying customers. The /stats command provides concrete evidence that requests to gemini-3.1-pro-preview are being counted against gemini-2.5-pro's quota, proving silent backend delegation. Users pay a premium price expecting specific model capabilities but receive degraded output quality. This is not a CLI bug per se but represents a significant service mismatch with financial impact.

source_issues.title: all gemini-3.1-pro-preview requests delegate to gemini-2.5-pro in background
source_issues.evidence: User paid for gemini-3.1-pro-preview access. /stats command shows identical usage percentage between gemini-3.1-pro-preview and gemini-2.5-pro (17%), proving backend routes all requests to 2.5-pro. User explicitly states 'I paid for gemini-3.1-pro-preview access because it's the most capable model for complex code tasks.' Response delay and logic faults align with weaker model.

signals.topic: Resume command references invalid session identifier after resuming a session

Running the printed command fails with 'Invalid session identifier', trapping users in a loop and making session history inaccessible.
aliases: Session resume prints wrong session ID
Resume command invalid after nested resume
Session history becomes inaccessible after resume
signals.review_reason: Session resume functionality is a core user workflow. When it prints an invalid session identifier, users cannot recover their conversation history and are trapped in a broken loop. The issue has clear reproduction steps and a concrete error message. This is a non-blocking but significant UX failure for a key persistence feature.

source_issues.title: fix resume command printed after quitting a resumed session
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction steps provided showing exact flow: resume sessionId1 -> quit -> prints 'gemini --resume sessionId2' -> resume sessionId2 -> quit -> prints invalid identifier. Clear error message: 'Error resuming session: Invalid session identifier'. Goodbye footer and session summary get out of sync with actual resumed conversation ID.

signals.topic: ToolSerializer.dumps f-string brace bug produces literal '{e}' instead of actual exception details, making pickle serialization failures undebuggable

signals.review_reason: This is a bug that directly degrades the debugging experience: when pickle serialization fails inside the agent, users receive a literal '{e}' string instead of the actual exception, making it impossible to understand what went wrong. source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message

source_issues.title: Save/Load agent memory

signals.topic: Subagent invocation drops runtime config — context, model switch, and tracing callbacks not propagated to subagents
signals.summary: The task tool's subagent invocations (via SubAgentMiddleware) call subagent.invoke/ainvoke without forwarding the parent's RunnableConfig. This causes subagent tools to receive runtime.context=None, breaks CLI model switching for subagents, and silently drops Langfuse/LangSmith tracing callbacks and metadata.
aliases: runtime config not passed to subagent invocations
model switch not propagated to subagents
config not forwarded to subagent invocations
signals.review_reason: Three independent external users confirm the same root cause: SubAgentMiddleware does not forward RunnableConfig to subagent.invoke/ainvoke. This blocks three distinct high-value workflows: (1) subagent tools receiving runtime context, (2) CLI model switching applying to subagents, (3) Langfuse/LangSmith tracing subagent LLM calls. Each is a main-flow functional failure, not an edge case. count=3 meets P1 threshold with strong evidence.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware regression — runtime config not passed to subagent invocations (PR #602 fix lost in #1041 refactor)
source_issues.evidence: runtime.context = None in subagent tools after PR #1041 rewrote subagents.py; subagent.invoke/ainvoke called without forwarding runtime.config; reproducible with minimal example

source_issues.title: Model switch not propagated to subagents

signals.topic: Windows platform UnicodeDecodeError crashes in CLI server startup and SDK backends
signals.summary: Multiple locations in the codebase use open() or subprocess without explicit encoding parameters, causing UnicodeDecodeError crashes on Windows where the default text encoding is GBK/cp936. Affected paths include CLI server lifespan (server fails to start), FilesystemBackend.read (agent tool crashes), and LocalShellBackend.execute (subprocess reader thread crashes with data loss).
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues across CLI and SDK layers all involve the same root cause: missing explicit encoding='utf-8' in file/subprocess operations. On Windows (GBK default), these cause server startup failure (blocking CLI entirely), agent tool crashes (blocking file read), and subprocess reader thread crashes with silent data loss. Each is a main-flow failure with a clear stack trace. count=3 meets P1 threshold.

signals.topic: Compaction strategies produce incorrect message grouping — models receive wrong context
signals.summary: Running the compaction sample shows multiple failures: only one tool call is compacted instead of two, user messages are incorrectly grouped by tool_result_compaction, and the model receives more message groups than expected. The compaction logic incorrectly identifies which messages to group together, resulting in wrong context being sent to the model.
signals.review_reason: Compaction is a core feature for managing context windows in long-running agent conversations. When compaction logic is wrong, the model receives incorrect message groupings, which degrades the quality of responses and can lead to confused or incorrect agent behavior. This is a functional correctness bug that directly affects the quality of agent outputs, though it does not completely block workflow execution.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Compaction strategies seem incorrect
source_issues.evidence: Running the compaction sample shows multiple failures: only one tool call is compacted instead of two, user messages are incorrectly grouped by tool_result_compaction, and the model receives more message groups than expected. The compaction logic incorrectly identifies which messages to group together, resulting in wrong context being sent to the model.

signals.topic: Tool approval workflow broken for sub-agents — approval response does not resume inner tool execution
signals.summary: When a sub-agent is used via .as_tool() and its inner tool requires approval_mode='always_require', the approval request correctly propagates to the caller, but after the caller sends the approval response and the workflow attempts to resume, the inner tool is never executed. The approval response is lost and the tool call is silently skipped.
aliases: sub-agent tool approval does not work
approval response lost for nested agent tools
signals.review_reason: The tool approval security feature is broken for sub-agents: approval requests propagate correctly to the caller, but after the approval is given the tool is never executed. This is a functional gap that makes approval_mode='always_require' unreliable for any workflow using sub-agents via .as_tool(), defeating the purpose of the security control.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Cannot approve tool usage from sub-agents
source_issues.evidence: When a sub-agent is used via .as_tool() and its inner tool requires approval_mode='always_require', the approval request correctly propagates to the caller, but after the caller sends the approval response and the workflow attempts to resume, the inner tool is never executed. The approval response is lost and the tool call is silently skipped.

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat livelock when allow_repeated_speaker=False: fallback returns excluded previous speaker causing infinite loop
signals.summary: When SelectorGroupChat's LLM-based speaker selector exhausts max_selector_attempts with allow_repeated_speaker=False, the fallback logic incorrectly returns self._previous_speaker — the exact speaker that was supposed to be excluded. This causes a livelock where the same agent repeats indefinitely, burning credits and blocking task completion.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed livelock bug with clear reproduction path: allow_repeated_speaker=False is violated by the fallback logic in _selector_group_chat.py, returning the excluded previous speaker and causing an infinite loop. This is a workflow runtime issue that blocks task completion and burns API credits. count=1, single repo. Marked P2 rather than P0 because count=1 with no corroborating reports in this dataset.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: Bug: fallback returns self._previous_speaker instead of excluding it. When allow_repeated_speaker=False and the LLM consistently selects the previous speaker across all max_selector_attempts, the fallback returns the excluded speaker, causing an infinite loop where the same agent speaks repeatedly. Root cause identified in _selector_group_chat.py: fallback returns previous_speaker unconditionally when selector attempts are exhausted.

signals.topic: ffmpeg child process orphaned and hangs when no video frames are recorded
signals.summary: When video recording captures no frames (e.g., navigation to blank page or immediate navigation away), ffmpeg process is not properly terminated. The Node.js parent process hangs indefinitely waiting on stdin that ffmpeg will never close, causing resource leaks and test hangs.
signals.review_reason: Indefinite process hang is a workflow-blocking runtime failure. Affects real production users (Cloudflare telescope) and blocks automated test suites. Both chromium.launch and chromium.launchPersistentContext are affected as they share the video recording code path. The fix exists in main but is not yet released to stable.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ffmpeg orphaned if no frames are recorded
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script hangs indefinitely. User reports this is causing intermittent hangs in production at cloudflare/telescope. Fixed in main (commit d039c403) but users on 1.58.2 still affected. Workaround requires manual process termination.

signals.topic: Test run with workers=0 silently succeeds without running any tests, creating false-positive CI results
signals.summary: When Playwright test runner is invoked with workers=0 or negative values, the process exits with code 0 (success) even though no tests actually run. This creates false-positive signals in CI pipelines, allowing broken test suites to pass silently.
signals.review_reason: False positive CI results are a critical quality gate failure. The bug allows broken test suites to pass silently, which defeats the entire purpose of automated testing. The comparison to forbidOnly demonstrates the expected safe behavior — zero workers should fail, not pass. While count=1, the CI impact and clear user-visible harm warrant P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Test run with parameter workers=0 (or a negative number) is treated as successful
source_issues.evidence: Author explicitly states this affects CI pipelines: 'I would expect the same behavior as with forbidOnly - the entire test run should be marked as failed to prevent false positives in CI pipelines.' No tests execute but process exits with success code.

signals.topic: playwright install fails in sandboxed environments due to Node.js resolving proxy hostname via local DNS instead of delegating to proxy
signals.summary: In sandboxed/restricted environments (e.g., Claude Code remote sandbox) where direct DNS resolution is blocked and all outbound traffic must go through an HTTP proxy, playwright install fails with EAI_AGAIN because Node.js resolves the proxy hostname locally before establishing the tunnel connection. This blocks the fundamental setup step of installing browsers.
signals.review_reason: Blocks the fundamental 'playwright install' workflow in sandboxed/CI environments that route all traffic through HTTP proxies with DNS-only resolution. Users must resort to manual browser downloads as a workaround, which is not acceptable for automated setups. The bug is in Playwright's own download infrastructure (browserFetcher.js + network.js), not a Node.js limitation that cannot be worked around.

source_issues.title: playwright install fails in Claude Code Sandbox
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis provided: HttpsProxyAgent resolves proxy hostname via local DNS (node:internal/dns/promises) before establishing CONNECT tunnel. This creates a circular dependency in DNS-restricted environments. HTTPS_PROXY is correctly set. Workaround requires manual curl download and manual unzip to ~/.cache/ms-playwright/.

signals.topic: electron.launch() fails on Electron 40.2.1 with 'bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0' preventing Playwright from controlling Electron apps
signals.summary: On Electron 40.2.1, electron.launch() fails before application code runs because Playwright passes --remote-debugging-port=0 as a CLI argument which Electron 40.2.1 rejects.
