A previous fix attempt (#39012) was reverted due to regressions with VS Code/Electron 39, leaving the issue unresolved for Electron 40.x users.
signals.review_reason: Complete API failure of electron.launch() blocks the entire Electron testing workflow. The fact that a fix was attempted and then reverted, with no replacement yet shipped, means this remains a known unresolved regression for Electron 40.x users. Count=1 but it completely blocks main functionality for a supported Electron version.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: electron.launch() still fails on Electron 40.2.1 after revert of #39012
source_issues.evidence: electron.launch() fails with 'bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0' before any application code runs. Affects the standard npm electron package at 40.2.1. The previous fix was reverted. User notes they must maintain a local Playwright patch just to use electron.launch() on current Electron versions.

signals.topic: Playwright Test for VSCode Extension fails to discover tests in code using pure ESM packages (no CommonJS export)
signals.summary: The Playwright Test VSCode extension's test explorer does not discover tests when the code under test contains pure ESM npm packages that have no CommonJS export. The same tests run successfully via npx from the terminal, but the VSCode integration fails silently with a require() of ES Module error.
signals.review_reason: Breaks the VSCode test discovery workflow for projects using ESM-only packages, a common pattern in modern Node.js projects using vite. The error message is cryptic and causes tests to be invisible in the IDE even though they run fine from CLI. Impact is developer-experience degradation rather than total workflow blockage, hence P2.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright Test for VSCode Extension does not discover tests when pure ESM packages are used in code
source_issues.evidence: Error: require() of ES Module from intl-messageformat not supported. Tests run via npx but VSCode test explorer fails to list them. User uses vite as build tool. This breaks the primary development workflow for any project using ESM-only packages.

signals.topic: AgentGroupChat fails with "Unknown response format <class 'dict'>" when Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor (OpenTelemetry instrumentation) is enabled, AgentGroupChat with AzureAIAgent fails immediately because the telemetry instrumentor does not support `dict` type for `response_format`, raising a ValueError that blocks all multi-agent executions.
signals.review_reason: 用户主流程被完全阻断：启用 Azure Monitor 后，所有 AgentGroupChat 执行立即失败并抛出 ValueError，自动重试全部失败。这是明确的主流程阻断场景，遥测 instrumentation 本不应该破坏执行流程。

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with "Unknown response format <class 'dict'>" when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: Unknown response format <class 'dict'> — all agent executions fail, automatic retries all fail, multi-agent flow is completely blocked. Platform: Python 3.11, semantic-kernel[azure]==1.39.2, azure-monitor-opentelemetry==1.8.6.

signals.topic: ChatHistorySummarizationReducer does not reduce history — full conversation is sent to LLM on every call
signals.summary: The ChatHistorySummarizationReducer is configured with target_count=3 and auto_reduce=True, but the complete chat history is still passed to the LLM API on every call, defeating its purpose and causing significant token waste and cost overhead in multi-turn, multi-agent scenarios.
aliases: Full chat history passed to LLM instead of summary
signals.review_reason: 关键计费异常持续发生：ChatHistorySummarizationReducer 配置正确但完全不工作，所有多轮对话都以完整历史发送给 LLM，直接导致 token 费用浪费。在 GroupChatOrchestration 多智能体场景下影响尤为严重，用户主动配置了 summarizer 但毫无效果。

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Complete chat history is getting passed to LLM - chat history summarizer is not working
source_issues.evidence: ChatHistorySummarizationReducer with auto_reduce=True still passes full chat history to LLM on every call. Reproduced in GroupChatOrchestration with multiple agents. Results in ongoing token waste and cost loss in multi-turn conversations.

signals.topic: McpTool import fails in semantic-kernel[Azure] due to azure-ai-agents dependency version mismatch
signals.summary: The semantic-kernel[Azure] extra depends on azure-ai-agents beta versions where McpTool existed, but the released azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 (August) no longer exports McpTool, causing import failures for users who upgrade.
aliases: McpTool import missing after azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 release
Missing McpTool due to azure-ai-agents version
signals.review_reason: 关键 MCP 功能完全不可用：azure-ai-agents 从 beta 升级到 GA 1.1.0 后 McpTool 被移除，导致所有依赖该导入的用户无法使用 MCP 工具。这是版本依赖管理失误造成的关键功能缺失，影响使用 MCP 集成的所有用户。

source_issues.title: Bug: Python - Semantic Kernel 1.35.1 is missing McpTools due to azure-ai-agents 1.1.0
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to semantic-kernel[Azure]>=1.35.1, `from azure.ai.agents.models import McpTool` fails because the GA release of azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 removed McpTool that existed in beta. McpTool is a core MCP integration component.

signals.topic: MCP tool names with dashes cause System.ArgumentException when converting to Kernel Functions (.NET)
signals.summary: When MCP servers expose tools with dashes in their names (e.g., 'create-pages'), converting them to Kernel Functions throws System.ArgumentException because dashes are not valid in plugin names, with no automatic workaround provided.
aliases: .NET MCP tool name dash not allowed
Plugin name validation rejects MCP tool names with dashes
signals.review_reason: 常见 MCP 工具名称与 SK 不兼容导致工作流完全中断：dash 分隔的工具名（如 'create-pages'）是 MCP 生态的常见实践，但 SK 的插件名验证直接拒绝这些名称，用户无法将 MCP 工具接入 SK，没有任何 workaround 被提供。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Converting MCP Tools to Kernel Function Throws System.ArgumentException
source_issues.evidence: MCP server exposes 'create-pages' tool; calling mcpClient.ListToolsAsync() then aiFunction.AsKernelFunction() throws ArgumentException: 'A plugin name can contain only ASCII letters, digits, and underscores: create-pages is not a valid name'. NuGet 1.61.0, .NET, Mac OS.

signals.topic: C# + SK sending Unicode encoding to QWEN LLM causes LLM to reply in Unicode, wasting tokens
signals.summary: When using C# and Semantic Kernel to call QWEN (Alibaba) LLM, the HTTP request interceptor shows the request is sent as Unicode, causing the LLM to respond in Unicode format as well, resulting in significant token waste and severely degraded reply efficiency.
aliases: QWEN Unicode encoding causing token waste in C#
C# HTTP request encoding causing LLM to output Unicode
signals.review_reason: 持续性 token 费用浪费：QWEN 模型调用时 Unicode 编码问题导致 LLM 回复也使用 Unicode，直接浪费 token 费用并降低回复效率。用户明确表示这是一个严重影响效率的 bug，且 bug 曾被关闭后又被用户要求重新打开，表明问题未得到妥善解决。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: When using C # and SK to call QWEN, I used the request interceptor of httpclient. I found that when it was sent to LLM, it was Unicode, which caused LLM to also reply using Unicode, resulting in a lot of token waste and seriously affecting reply efficiency.
source_issues.evidence: HTTP request interceptor in C# reveals that the payload sent to QWEN LLM is encoded in Unicode format, causing the model to respond in Unicode characters. This wastes tokens and degrades efficiency. Bug was closed then reopened by user asking not to blindly close important bugs.

signals.topic: Windows: Python executable not found by Codex tool calls despite being in PATH
signals.summary: On Windows, Codex fails to invoke `python` via tool calls even when the executable is in the user's PATH, causing 'not recognized' errors. This blocks the primary code execution workflow on Windows.
aliases: python command not found on Windows
python tool call fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: Python tool execution failure on Windows directly blocks the primary coding workflow. While only 1 report, the impact is severe — a core tool (python execution) silently fails on a major platform. The evidence shows a clear PATH mismatch where the shell finds python but Codex's subprocess spawn does not.

source_issues.title: Codex cannot call python.
source_issues.evidence: User reports python is in PATH and callable normally via shell, but Codex tool call fails with 'The term python is not recognized'. This is a main workflow blocker on Windows — Python execution is a core Codex use case.

signals.topic: app-server hangs after emitting tool calls since v0.117.0 (regression)
signals.summary: Codex app-server becomes unresponsive/stuck after emitting tool calls since version 0.117.0+, affecting both Windows x64 and cross-platform environments. Rolling back to 0.116.0 resolves the issue.
aliases: app-server stuck after tool calls regression
codex app-server not responding after tool calls 0.117.0
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression introduced in 0.117.0 that makes the app-server completely unresponsive after tool call emission. This is a severe main-flow block affecting all Codex app-server users. The clear regression signal (works on 0.116.0, broken on 0.117.0 and 0.118.0) makes this a high-confidence, high-impact issue.

source_issues.title: codex app-server is broken since 0.117.0+ after it emits some tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression in 0.117.0 and 0.118.0 on Windows x64. User provides session ID and explicitly confirms reverting to 0.116.0 fixes the issue. This blocks the entire Codex app-server workflow — the main execution engine becomes non-functional after any tool call emission.

signals.topic: Windows: websocket transport times out (~15s) before falling back to HTTP, causing severe response delays
signals.summary: On Windows, Codex CLI's websocket transport repeatedly times out (~15s per attempt) for up to 5 retries before falling back to HTTP, which succeeds. This creates a multi-minute delay per session start on affected Windows machines.
signals.review_reason: Severe UX degradation on Windows — websocket timeouts cause 15s+ stalls per attempt with 5 retries before fallback. While the workflow eventually completes via HTTP, this is a significant per-session delay that wastes user time on every interaction start. Logs provide concrete evidence of the failure pattern.

source_issues.title: Windows: responses_websocket connect to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses times out while responses_http succeeds
source_issues.evidence: User provides trace logs showing websocket connect timeout of 15015ms with success=false. After 5 retries (~75 seconds of stall), HTTP fallback succeeds. Enterprise user on Windows 11. Affects every session start where websocket is selected.

signals.topic: Unexpected rapid token/subscription burn causing early weekly limit exhaustion
signals.summary: Users report token consumption far exceeding expected usage, causing weekly API limits to be reached much faster than normal. Affects paid Plus and Pro subscribers with real cost implications.
signals.review_reason: Real cost impact — user reports hitting weekly limit significantly faster despite lighter usage, implying Codex may be consuming tokens beyond expected amounts. This is a billing/cost issue with direct financial harm to users. While only 1 report, the explicit cost impact qualifies it as a pain point.

source_issues.title: token burn
source_issues.evidence: User reports reaching weekly limit 'twice as fast as ever before with lighter use.' User provides thread session ID as evidence. Clear cost/billing impact for a Plus subscriber.

signals.topic: MCP bootstrap fails with SOCKS-only proxy (ALL_PROXY) causing fatal startup error
signals.summary: codex_apps MCP bootstrap fails when Codex is configured with SOCKS-only proxy (ALL_PROXY=socks5h://) because the reqwest client lacks the socks feature, emitting a fatal 'Transport channel closed' error during startup.
signals.review_reason: SOCKS proxy users cannot use the codex_apps MCP bootstrap feature, getting fatal startup errors. The issue is well-documented with root cause analysis showing reqwest is compiled without the socks feature. This blocks MCP workflow for SOCKS users and creates noisy fatal errors during startup.

source_issues.title: codex_apps MCP bootstrap fails on SOCKS-only ALL_PROXY and appears to require HTTP proxy vars
source_issues.evidence: User provides detailed technical analysis with code references (reqwest without socks feature). Reproduction steps show fatal 'TunnelUnexpectedEof' error. Documents that main ping works but optional MCP bootstrap crashes with fatal error, polluting logs and indicating incomplete SOCKS support.

signals.topic: hydrate_from_state stores ephemeral object id() causing false-positive dedup and 400 API errors in HITL workflows
signals.summary: When OpenAIServerConversationTracker.hydrate_from_state resumes a run, it stores id() of temporary dict objects (created by ItemHelpers.input_to_new_input_list) in sent_items without keeping a strong reference. After GC, CPython reuses the same memory address for new dicts (e.g. HITL rejection function_call_output), causing prepare_input to incorrectly treat them as 'already sent' and drop them. This results in a 400 'No tool output found for function call' API error, completely breaking tool-use flows in any resumed/human-in-the-loop scenario.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-path blocking bug. The core agent tool-call loop with human-in-the-loop (HITL) rejection is completely broken — the tool output gets silently dropped after resume, producing a 400 API error. A deterministic self-contained repro script is provided proving the GC id() collision. This blocks any production agent using resume/HITL workflows.

source_issues.title: hydrate_from_state stores id() of ephemeral objects in sent_items, causing false-positive dedup after GC
source_issues.evidence: Bug is reproducible with a self-contained script: id() of a GC'd temp dict collides with a later rejection function_call_output dict, prepare_input returns 0 items, leading to 400 'No tool output found for function call'. SDK v0.13.1, Python 3.12.8. Explicit root cause identified in oai_conversation.py hydrate_from_state.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when base64 file inputs are introduced, causing significant cost increase
signals.summary: When using Agents SDK with prompt caching enabled (cache hit ~96.7%), adding a single base64-encoded file input to the prompt causes the cache hit rate to drop to 0% on that round, even though all static prefix content (system instructions, tool definitions) remains unchanged. This is observed consistently across both the Agents SDK and the Responses API directly, indicating the cache key computation is disrupted by file inputs. The impact is direct cost increase for any production agent workflow that mixes text and file inputs.
signals.review_reason: Significant cost impact for production users. Cache hit dropping from 96.7% to 0% on every first file-input round means users pay full price for repeated file-heavy requests. While the root cause may partially reside in the upstream API, the Agents SDK is the interface users interact with, and the documentation/setup leads users to expect caching to work. The issue is explicitly labeled as a question and needs-more-info, but the user has provided concrete benchmark data and a clear expected behavior — the zero-cache behavior is clearly unexpected and costly.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: User reports consistent cache behavior: text-only rounds = 96.7% cache hit, first file-input round = 0% cache hit, repeating the same file input restores cache to 90.3%. Identical behavior observed in both Agents SDK and Responses API directly. Prompts use prompt_cache_key and exceed 1024 token threshold. The user explicitly asks whether this is expected behavior or a bug, noting the shared prefix/instructions/tools are unchanged.

signals.topic: SDK rejects image_url type for base64 images when Chat Completions API is configured, blocking image input workflow
signals.summary: When the SDK is configured to use Chat Completions API (set_default_openai_api('chat_completions')), it still validates and rejects messages with type: image_url (the standard Chat Completions format) and only accepts input_image (Responses API format). This prevents users from sending base64-encoded images when using Azure OpenAI or other Chat Completions-compatible endpoints, since the standard message format is rejected at SDK validation before any API call is made.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the image input workflow entirely for users of Chat Completions API mode. The SDK validates input format internally and rejects the standard Chat Completions image_url type, forcing users into a format that the API doesn't accept. This is a workflow-breaking bug for any user trying to send images via Azure OpenAI or similar Chat Completions endpoints.

source_issues.title: Error when sending base64 image with type: image_url to Chat Completions API
source_issues.evidence: User configures Azure OpenAI with set_default_openai_api('chat_completions'), the request is blocked at SDK-level validation before reaching the API. Workaround of using input_image type works for the SDK but breaks at the API side since Chat Completions does not support that format. SDK versions: openai 2.29.0, openai-agents 0.13.0.

signals.topic: griffe vs griffelib version conflict causes ImportError, blocking CI and service startup
signals.summary: A version conflict between griffe (1.15.0) and griffelib (2.0.0) causes an ImportError when importing the agents module. The conflict arises because the two packages can overwrite each other depending on installation order, leading to missing exports in griffe._internal.expressions. This breaks CI pipelines and prevents services from starting.
signals.review_reason: This causes CI pipeline failures and prevents the service from starting at all — a complete startup crash. The root cause is a dependency version conflict that the SDK's dependency specification doesn't adequately guard against. This is a blocking issue for any deployment environment where both packages are present.

source_issues.title: maybe use griffelib instead of griffe as dependency, and update to 2+
source_issues.evidence: User's CI and service crash on import with: ImportError: cannot import name 'ExprInterpolation' from 'griffe._internal.expressions'. Root cause is version conflict between griffe 1.15.0 and griffelib 2.0.0, which can overwrite each other based on installation order. Running on Python 3.13.12.

signals.topic: AnyLLMModel pydantic validation fails when using multiple rounds of tool calls due to input type mismatch
signals.summary: When using AnyLLMModel through multiple rounds of tool calls, pydantic validation fails because some versions of any-llm's ResponsesParams.input field only accepts str, but after multiple rounds of dialogue the input becomes list[TResponseInputItem]. This causes a pydantic validation error that blocks the multi-turn tool-call workflow.
signals.review_reason: This blocks multi-turn tool-call workflows when using AnyLLMModel. The pydantic validation error causes the extension to fail at runtime after the first tool-call round, making the feature unusable for production multi-turn agentic workflows. 6 comments confirm community interest and the issue was closed after a workaround was found.

source_issues.title: AnyLLMModel failed ResponsePalms validation during multiple rounds of tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Author provides a subclass fix overriding _make_any_llm_responses_params to bypass pydantic validation, explicitly identifying the root cause: after multiple tool-call rounds, input transitions from str to list[TResponseInputItem], causing pydantic validation error. 6 comments indicate community interest. Closed with the workaround.

signals.topic: Responses WebSocket 连接因小数 temperature 值异常关闭（code 1000，无任何事件返回）
signals.summary: 当 Responses API WebSocket 连接中 temperature 参数传入小数（如 1.2）时，连接立即以 code 1000 关闭且不产生任何事件，导致实时流式响应主流程完全阻断。用户必须在 0-1 整数范围内才能正常使用。
aliases: Responses API WebSocket failure with fractional temperature
signals.review_reason: WebSocket 连接因小数 temperature 立即以 code 1000 关闭且零事件返回，属于主流程阻断性 bug。用户提供可复现脚本和评论互动（3条），确认问题真实存在，影响所有使用 Responses WebSocket 且传入小数 temperature 的用户。符合痛点定义：主流程失败/阻断。count=1 不足以 P0，但应保留为 P1。

source_issues.title: Responses WebSocket (/v1/responses) closes with code 1000 and no events when temperature is a decimal (e.g., 1.2)
source_issues.evidence: WebSocket connection to wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses 立即以 code 1000 关闭，events=[]，整数 temperature 正常工作，小数 temperature 导致主流程完全阻断。用户提供了可复现脚本，3 条评论确认问题存在。

signals.topic: Config agent 'args' field silently ignored — commands requiring arguments fail silently
signals.summary: When users configure agents with a 'command' plus 'args' array in ~/.acpx/config.json, the args are silently discarded at runtime. The agent process spawns without intended arguments, causing ACP protocol initialization to hang. Users have no indication that args were ignored.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：配置了args的agent命令静默失败，用户完全无法感知问题根源。ACP协议初始化挂起意味着整个agent交互不可用。提供明确复现步骤、代码根因和影响范围，置信度高。

source_issues.title: fix: parseAgents() ignores 'args' field in ~/.acpx/config.json agents config
source_issues.evidence: parseAgents() only reads raw.command and discards raw.args. Agent with args silently starts without correct arguments, ACP protocol init hangs. Multiple agent versions affected (0.3.1, 0.4.0, latest main).

signals.topic: Windows Node.js v22 agent spawn fails with EINVAL — all ACP agent commands broken
signals.summary: On Windows with Node.js v22.12+, child_process.spawn() returns EINVAL when trying to execute .cmd/.ps1 wrapper scripts (npx, node, all npm-installed CLIs) without shell:true. All agent commands (Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Gemini) are completely broken with no workaround.
aliases: shell:true missing on Windows agent spawn
signals.review_reason: 高影响平台阻断：所有Windows + Node.js v22用户的全部agent命令彻底不可用（EINVAL），无任何agent可正常工作。影响范围覆盖所有ACP agent（Codex/Claude/OpenCode/Gemini），且用户唯一解法是降级Node或切换HTTP模式，严重损害核心体验。

source_issues.title: Bug: spawn EINVAL on Windows with Node.js v22 — all agent commands fail
source_issues.evidence: Node.js v22.12+ security change causes EINVAL when spawning .cmd/.ps1 without shell:true. ALL agent commands fail (npx, node, npm CLIs). Only workaround is HTTP API mode or downgrade to Node v20.

source_issues.title: Windows: terminal commands fail with ENOENT because buildTerminalSpawnOptions lacks shell:true
source_issues.evidence: Separate code path (terminal spawn) also missing shell:true on Windows, causing all terminal commands (git, node, etc.) to fail with ENOENT. Fix pattern identical to issue #191.

signals.topic: macOS persistent sessions go dead immediately after creation — 'queue owner unavailable'
signals.summary: On macOS, persistent acpx sessions are created successfully but immediately report dead/queue owner unavailable on status checks. Sessions loop in a dead state with no recovery. Thread-bound ACP sessions are unstable; users must fall back to one-shot mode.
signals.review_reason: 主流程部分阻断：macOS用户的persistent session完全不可用（立刻dead），thread-bound ACP session生态崩溃。用户被迫降级到one-shot模式，核心功能降级。问题可稳定复现，影响多种acpx adapter版本。

source_issues.title: Persistent sessions become dead immediately (queue owner unavailable) on macOS
source_issues.evidence: sessions ensure succeeds but status immediately shows dead/queue owner unavailable. Affects multiple acpx adapter versions and both arm64/x86 macOS hardware. No workaround except switching to one-shot mode (mode: run, thread: false).

signals.topic: ACP protocolVersion type mismatch breaks Gemini CLI integration
signals.summary: acpx sends protocolVersion as string "1.0" but Gemini CLI expects number 1. The ACP handshake fails with JSON-RPC -32603 error, making Gemini CLI ACP mode completely unusable with acpx.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Gemini CLI的ACP集成完全失败（协议握手直接报错），用户无法通过acpx使用Gemini CLI。提供明确复现命令、错误信息和根因分析，是明确的跨agent互操作性问题。

source_issues.title: ACP: protocolVersion type mismatch with Gemini CLI (--acp)
source_issues.evidence: acpx sends protocolVersion: "1.0" (string) but Gemini CLI expects protocolVersion: 1 (number). Handshake fails with -32603 Internal error. Codex and Claude work fine; only Gemini is blocked.

signals.topic: Gateway restart causes session spawn to silently fail — error swallowing and null misinterpretation prevent recovery
signals.summary: After a gateway restart, ACP sessions permanently fail to start. Exit code 3 (TIMEOUT) is silently swallowed: createNamedSession returns null, ensureSession passes null upward, and recoverEnsureFailure misinterprets null as 'session already exists'. This creates an infinite dead-session recovery loop with zero sessions ever recovering.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：gateway重启后所有ACP session永远无法恢复，进入死循环。错误在三层代码中被静默吞掉，用户看不到任何有意义的信息。recoverEnsureFailure将null错误当作'成功'处理，导致系统状态完全错误。

source_issues.title: ACP session spawn fails silently after gateway restart — error swallowing leads to dead session loop
source_issues.evidence: Three-layer error swallowing: createNamedSession returns null on all errors, ensureSession passes null, recoverEnsureFailure counts null as success. After restart, all sessions enter infinite dead-loop: acp startup identity reconcile shows resolved=0 failed=N. Exit code 3 (TIMEOUT) is discarded at every layer.

signals.topic: Overly aggressive security scanning generates high volume of false-positive suspicious flags on benign skills
signals.summary: The ClawHub security scanner (VirusTotal + OpenClaw analysis) incorrectly flags a large number of legitimate, benign skills as suspicious, blocking them from the marketplace and requiring publishers to go through a manual appeal process. Patterns detected as suspicious include: legitimate API endpoints, local file access for user data, cron job registration, token storage for authenticated services, and network calls to the skill's own documented backend.
aliases: Benign skills incorrectly flagged as suspicious
False positive security detections blocking legitimate marketplace listings
Scanner heuristic causing false suspicious classifications
Manual appeal bottleneck due to scanner false positives
signals.review_reason: 15 out of 20 issues in this dataset are false-positive security scan appeals — a 75% false positive rate on the affected skills. These are not security vulnerabilities but legitimate, benign skills (TTS, trading APIs, NAS management, penetration testing tools, booking managers, document processors, emotional companions) blocked from the marketplace by overly broad heuristic detection. The scan flags benign patterns: local file access for user data, cron registration via official API, token storage for documented services, shell scripts calling curl/jq, and network calls to a skill's own declared backend. Users must go through a manual GitHub issue appeal process to get each skill re-reviewed, creating a significant publishing bottleneck. At least 2 skills explicitly report OpenClaw's own scan rating as 'Benign (high confidence)' while the platform still displays a suspicious flag.

source_issues.title: False positive: ClawStreet skill flagged for legitimate API endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Skill publishes legitimate REST API endpoints (market status, stock quotes, trade execution) for a trading platform. All URLs are the skill's own documented API. Pattern detected: remote URL references in SKILL.md — identical to any API-based skill.

source_issues.title: Methodalgo Market Intel Explorer skill incorrectly flagged
source_issues.evidence: Publisher spent significant effort remediating 5 distinct flagged categories (CREDENTIALS, INSTRUCTION SCOPE, PURPOSE & CAPABILITY, INSTALL MECHANISM). Still flagged despite full compliance.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] lobster-says v1.1.0 — legitimate emotional companion skill
source_issues.evidence: Skill flagged for: local file access (~/.openclaw sessions), remote server POST to nixiashuo.com (its own backend), cron registration, token storage. VirusTotal: 0/60 detections. OpenClaw: Benign (medium). Multiple legitimate behaviors individually trigger suspicious flags.

source_issues.title: Sonarbay-skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: News CLI skill incorrectly flagged. Minimal issue body but clearly a false positive appeal.

source_issues.title: Appeal for Security Reclassification of loveclaw on ClawHub
source_issues.evidence: Flagged for: child_process (execFileSync for openclaw CLI cron), workspace .env reading (allowlisted keys only), remote API calls (documented cloud service). Maintainer implemented extensive security hardening and risk disclosures.

source_issues.title: Skill marked as suspicious: fnnas-download
source_issues.evidence: SSH-based NAS management skill using user-controlled SSH keys (no passwords, no hardcoded credentials, no external connections). Legitimate local network tool incorrectly flagged.

source_issues.title: Credential Auditor Skill Incorrectly Flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Natural language to opencli command skill. Reuses Chrome browser login session — no passwords or API keys exposed. Legal warnings in SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE.

source_issues.title: Credential Auditor Skill Incorrectly Flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Legitimate penetration testing tool integrating Hydra, Medusa, Ncrack — standard Kali Linux security tools. No malicious code. Legal warnings present.

source_issues.title: Request review for recurring suspicious flag on wwt1995/triz-problem-solver
source_issues.evidence: Recurring flag despite OpenClaw rating: Benign (high confidence). VirusTotal only flagged. Remote endpoint explicitly disclosed in SKILL.md Data Handling notice. No arbitrary downloads, credential abuse, or persistence/escalation behavior.

source_issues.title: Skill marked as suspicious: skills-audit
source_issues.evidence: Skill is literally a security audit/rule-detection tool (blacklist matching for shell patterns, dynamic exec, base64, crontab, sensitive paths, network calls). Flagged for using the very patterns it documents as threats.

source_issues.title: booking-manager skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Booking management assistant connecting to databases and sending emails. References to credentials and API connections are intentional/necessary. VirusTotal: Benign.

source_issues.title: Skill marked as suspicious: mikrotik-routeros
source_issues.evidence: RouterOS management skill. VirusTotal: 0/60 detections. No security vendor flagged as malicious.

source_issues.title: ai-capability-analyzer has been incorrectly flagged
source_issues.evidence: One-line appeal confirming false positive.

source_issues.title: youtube-downloader-skill has been incorrectly flagged
source_issues.evidence: One-line appeal confirming false positive.

source_issues.title: Request to re-review / unflag skill ca-file-processor
source_issues.evidence: Local/offline document processing skill for CA firms (PDF, Excel, CSV, OCR). No credential harvesting, no unsafe actions. Still flagged.

source_issues.title: False positive: castreader skill flagged as suspicious despite benign scan results
source_issues.evidence: TTS web content extraction skill. OpenClaw: Benign (HIGH confidence). VirusTotal: Benign/Pending. All 7 remaining flagged patterns are functional necessities of any TTS skill (shell exec, env vars, file read + network send, browser control). Skill removed HTTP→HTTPS, removed --no-sandbox, deleted unused scripts — still flagged.

source_issues.title: MatchClaw skill marked as VirusTotal suspicious despite passing with 0/65
source_issues.evidence: VirusTotal: 0/65 detections when viewed directly, but ClawHub shows 'suspicious' flag. Secondary flag: required plugin download (legitimate dependency) and messenger API references (documented design). ClawHub UI and VirusTotal report are inconsistent.

signals.topic: User account broken state causes complete platform blockage (authentication and search failures)
signals.summary: At least one user's account is in a broken state causing authentication and plugin search to fail with server errors, completely blocking core platform usage.
aliases: Account in broken state blocking login
Authentication and search failures due to server errors
signals.review_reason: This is a single-user account-level platform blockage where both authentication and search — the two primary entry points — return server errors. While count=1, the severity is maximum: the user cannot use the platform at all. This meets the P0 exception criterion since review_reason provides unambiguous user impact evidence of total platform unavailability.

source_issues.title: My account is in a broken state, cannot authenticate or search plugins
source_issues.evidence: User reports [CONVEX M(users:ensure)] server error on login attempt, and plugin search returns 'Server Error'. Both core platform entry points are completely blocked.

signals.topic: Registry metadata extraction bug blocks skill publishing — openclaw.requires.env not parsed from published files
signals.summary: The clawhub publish CLI (v0.9.0) does not send openclaw.requires.env metadata to the registry server, causing the server-side scanner to see a mismatch between declared env vars (in SKILL.md/package.json) and registry metadata (empty). This results in benign skills being incorrectly flagged as suspicious.
aliases: Publish CLI payload missing env var metadata
clawhub publish CLI v0.9.0 metadata extraction failure
Env var declaration mismatch causing false suspicious flags
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed platform bug in the publish pipeline where CLI payload does not include required metadata fields, causing benign skills to be incorrectly blocked. The evidence includes root cause tracing (verified by deleting and re-publishing, trying JSON vs YAML, confirming CLI payload contents) and a direct comparison with a previously successful skill (deepread-ocr) using the identical format. The blocking is mechanical — not a false positive of the scanner itself but a data pipeline failure.

source_issues.title: False 'suspicious' flag: registry metadata not extracting openclaw.requires.env from published files
source_issues.evidence: Reporter verified that clawhub publish CLI v0.9.0 only sends slug/displayName/version/changelog/tags — not env var metadata. A skill published with identical metadata format as a previously benign-rated skill (deepread-ocr) was flagged suspicious solely due to the missing metadata extraction. Two skills (deepread-pii v2.0.0, deepread-byok v1.1.0) are blocked from the marketplace.

signals.topic: Cannot transfer skill ownership from personal account to organization account — slug collision error blocks workflow
signals.summary: The skill publish flow incorrectly treats a valid ownership transfer (user moving their own skill to an org they belong to) as a slug collision, preventing organizations from managing skills published by their members.
aliases: Skill ownership transfer blocked by false slug collision
Cannot reassign skill to organization publisher
Publisher ownership migration fails with slug taken error
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed code-level bug in convex/skills.ts where ownership transfer logic incorrectly treats a valid inter-publisher move as a collision. The reporter provides exact source location and logic. The workflow is completely blocked — the user cannot move their skill from a personal account to an organization they own, which prevents proper organizational management of published skills.

source_issues.title: Cannot change an existing skill's publisher/owner to an organization
source_issues.evidence: Reporter identifies exact root cause in convex/skills.ts: insertVersion compares skill.ownerPublisherId against the incoming ownerPublisherId and throws 'Slug is already taken' when they differ, even when the same user owns both the skill and the target org. Steps to reproduce: create org → publish skill under personal account → attempt to transfer to org → error. Blocks organization account adoption for skills.

signals.topic: Node mode fails to connect after enabling in settings — "Node Mode: Disconnected" shown despite gateway connection success
signals.summary: 用户启用 Node mode 并连接 gateway 后，状态显示 Connected 但 Node Mode 显示 Disconnected，且服务端未收到设备配对请求，主流程阻断
signals.review_reason: 用户启用 Node mode 是核心使用路径之一，连接 gateway 后 Node Mode 持续 Disconnected 且服务端无配对请求属于主流程阻断。Issue #114 有明确复现步骤、日志证据和社区确认，Repo Assist 进一步定位了两个根本原因（状态未重置、_isPendingApproval 未清除），修复后 503 项测试通过。count=1 且非高频，但有清晰的用户影响证据支撑，标记为 P1 而非 P0。

source_issues.title: Node mode not work
source_issues.evidence: 开启 Node mode 并连接 gateway 后状态显示 Connected 但 Node Mode: Disconnected；服务端无设备配对请求日志；被 Repo Assist 诊断出两个根本原因并通过 PR #115 修复

signals.topic: Quick Send / chat.send fails with "missing scope: operator.write" — 消息发送核心功能完全不可用
signals.summary: 用户使用内置 Quick Send 功能或自行开发的客户端发送消息均失败，日志显示 Gateway 返回 missing scope: operator.write，导致聊天消息发送主流程阻断
signals.review_reason: 聊天消息发送是应用的核心主流程。Quick Send 失败意味着用户既无法使用内置演示功能，也无法通过自定义客户端发送消息——主流程完全阻断。日志明确显示 Gateway 拒绝请求（missing scope），有用户实际影响证据。Repo Assist 定位根因为 handshake 缺少 operator.write scope，PR #113 已修复。非高频（count=1），但用户影响明确，标记 P1。

source_issues.title: I developed a client to send messages to openclaw, but it consistently fails to send. Even using the demo's quick send feature also fails to work
source_issues.evidence: 用户日志显示 QuickSend 消息发送失败：Gateway request failed: missing scope: operator.write；该 bug 同时影响内置 Quick Send 演示功能和用户自定义客户端；Repo Assist 诊断为 gateway 握手时缺少 operator.write scope 并通过 PR #113 修复

signals.topic: Tray menu overflow — 超出屏幕高度的菜单无法垂直滚动，部分菜单项不可访问
signals.summary: 当菜单项超出屏幕可显示范围时，托盘菜单不显示垂直滚动条，导致底部菜单项用户完全无法访问
signals.review_reason: 托盘菜单无法滚动导致部分菜单项不可访问，属于体验下降和关键功能可用性问题（多菜单项场景下阻断操作）。有明确 bug 标签和用户报告，PR #83 由社区提交修复。虽然 count=1、非高频，但 UI 可访问性问题明确，标记 P2。

source_issues.title: Overheight menu doesn't scroll vertically
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告菜单超出屏幕高度时无垂直滚动条，底部菜单项无法访问；Repo Assist 确认多显示器场景下 MonitorFromPoint 处理逻辑正确但滚动功能确实缺失；PR #83 已由社区提交修复

signals.topic: LiveSessionModelSwitchError causes task/session failures across isolated cron, spawned subagent, and session resume contexts
signals.summary: LiveSessionModelSwitchError causes automated workflows to fail and sessions to become unrecoverable across cron, subagent, and resume contexts
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking across 5 issues: isolated cron jobs fail (27+ jobs), spawned subagents fail before first attempt, session resume creates infinite error loops, and model fallback chain is completely defeated. User impact is severe - automated workflows stop functioning, sessions become unrecoverable, and fallback reliability is eliminated.

source_issues.title: LiveSessionModelSwitchError: isolated cron sessions inherit parent agent's model override
source_issues.evidence: ~27 cron jobs across 5 agents failing simultaneously; isolated sessions inherit parent model instead of starting fresh with payload model

source_issues.title: Session ending with assistant message causes infinite prefill error loop with Opus 4.6
source_issues.evidence: Sessions become permanently unrecoverable; 28 affected sessions across 16 agents in a single deployment; requires manual file deletion to recover

source_issues.title: Live model switch check prevents model fallback from working
source_issues.evidence: When primary model is overloaded, every fallback candidate is rejected before making an API call; fallback chain is completely defeated

source_issues.title: LiveSessionModelSwitchError in isolated cron jobs (v2026.3.28)
source_issues.evidence: ~25 of 33 cron jobs failing with LiveSessionModelSwitchError when using a different model than parent agent

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Spawned subagent with explicit model can fail before first attempt with LiveSessionModelSwitchError
source_issues.evidence: Spawned subagents with explicit model selection fail immediately before first model attempt; child task produces no output

signals.topic: Gateway silently drops messages or causes message duplication during provider outages and reconnects
signals.summary: Messages are either silently dropped or massively duplicated in the gateway retry loop
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - messages are either silently dropped (users get no response) or massively duplicated (tens of duplicates), causing severe UX degradation and context pollution. Three distinct but related failure modes in message delivery pipeline.

source_issues.title: Bug: Inbound messages re-delivered during API provider outage — missing message_id deduplication in gateway retry loop
source_issues.evidence: Single Telegram message delivered ~40 times during 15-minute API outage; retry loop re-delivers same message_id on every attempt without deduplication

source_issues.title: Gateway should log warning when message is dropped due to allow: false
source_issues.evidence: Messages silently dropped when channel config has allow:false; no log trail exists; messages lost for hours before detection; indistinguishable from routing bugs

source_issues.title: Slack DM: Embedded agent run not triggered when socket reconnects (stale-socket)
source_issues.evidence: Slack DMs silently dropped entirely when socket reconnects after stale-socket detection; no embedded_run triggered; user receives no response

signals.topic: Browser tools completely fail with AJV schema validation error on every invocation
signals.summary: All browser automation tools are completely non-functional due to AJV schema validation error
signals.review_reason: Critical feature unavailability - all browser automation tools (browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_run_code, etc.) are completely non-functional with 100% reproduction. This is a regression that blocks any workflow requiring browser interaction.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Browser tools fail with AJV "no schema with key or ref" 2020-12 error
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproduction rate for all browser tools (navigate, run_code, click, etc.); error occurs at parameter validation before tool executes; affects all channels using browser automation

signals.topic: Multi-agent routing resolves correct agent but creates session under wrong agent, loading wrong workspace and identity
signals.summary: Multi-agent routing identifies the correct agent but session creation uses the default agent, causing workspace/identity mismatch
signals.review_reason: Significant UX/cost impact - users interacting with a specific agent get routed to the wrong workspace with wrong identity and system prompts. This causes context confusion and data leakage between agent workspaces. Single repo but strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Multi-agent routing resolves correct agent but session is created under default agent
source_issues.evidence: When routing to non-default agent (e.g. second-ana), session key is built with 'main' as agent prefix; wrong workspace, identity files, and session store loaded; routing correctly identifies target agent but session creation loses the resolved agent ID

signals.topic: Auth profile failover does not distinguish dead API keys from rate limits, causing 30-90s latency per request
signals.summary: Expired API keys incur the same cooldown as transient rate limits, adding 30-90s overhead per request
signals.review_reason: Cost impact - dead API keys cause 30-90s overhead per request as gateway waits through cooldown before failing over. Scheduler jobs consistently timeout. Clear operational cost from misclassifying auth errors.

source_issues.title: Auth profile failover should differentiate 401 (dead key) from 429/529 (transient)
source_issues.evidence: Expired/invalid API key (401) enters same cooldown as rate limits; scheduler-dispatched jobs consistently timeout as gateway pings pong through dead key cooldown; each request incurs 30-90s overhead

signals.topic: Version incompatibility between litellm and openai/pydantic causes uncaught ImportError crashes
signals.summary: litellm's internal imports from openai.lib (_parsing, _pydantic) or pydantic_core (validate_core_schema) fail due to version conflicts, causing uncaught ImportError that crashes aider immediately on startup before any user interaction.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct version incompatibility scenarios (openai.lib/_parsing vs pydantic_core/validate_core_schema) both triggered via litellm import chain. Both cause immediate app crash with uncaught ImportError before user can perform any action. Multiple platforms affected (macOS). Root cause is litellm's fragile dependency chain pulling in conflicting versions of openai or pydantic.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in utils.py line 43
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name '_parsing' from 'openai.lib'. Crash in litellm when it imports openai internals. Platform: macOS Darwin 25.3.0.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in _core_utils.py line 9
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'validate_core_schema' from 'pydantic_core'. Version mismatch between pydantic and pydantic_core causes crash during litellm initialization. Platform: macOS Darwin 25.4.0.

signals.topic: Missing SSL certificate file crashes app startup (SSL_CERT_FILE env var points to non-existent file)
signals.summary: When the SSL_CERT_FILE environment variable points to a file that doesn't exist, litellm/httpx attempts to load it and crashes with FileNotFoundError in ssl.py, preventing the entire application from starting. This affects users on all platforms where SSL_CERT_FILE is set, frequently on Windows.
signals.review_reason: FileNotFoundError in ssl.py causes complete app startup failure before any user workflow can begin. The crash is uncaught and blocks the entire application. Issue remains open with recent comments, indicating an ongoing unresolved problem affecting users who have SSL_CERT_FILE set.

source_issues.title: Uncaught FileNotFoundError in ssl.py line 707
source_issues.evidence: FileNotFoundError in ssl.py line 707: 'cafile=os.environ["SSL_CERT_FILE"]' resolves to non-existent path. App crashes before any user workflow begins. Still open, recent activity 2026-03-30.

signals.topic: Missing litellm package crashes aider on startup with ModuleNotFoundError
signals.summary: When the litellm package is not installed in the Python environment, aider crashes with uncaught ModuleNotFoundError during model initialization, completely preventing app startup.
signals.review_reason: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError crashes the app during model initialization. While this is an environment setup issue, the lack of graceful error handling and clear messaging constitutes a poor user experience and blocks the primary workflow. The crash is uncaught, giving users a raw Python traceback with no actionable guidance.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in <frozen importlib._bootstrap> line 1004
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'. Aider crashes at startup during model validation. No graceful degradation or clear error message.

signals.topic: Missing scipy package crashes repo map generation with ModuleNotFoundError
signals.summary: When scipy is not installed, aider crashes with uncaught ModuleNotFoundError during pagerank computation in repo map generation, occurring mid-workflow after the app has started successfully.
signals.review_reason: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError crashes the app during a core workflow (repo map generation via pagerank). Affects the primary use case of aider for code-aware assistance. While scipy is technically optional for enhanced repo mapping, the crash occurs in the main conversation loop with no graceful fallback, blocking the user's current task.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in pagerank_alg.py line 454
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scipy'. Crash occurs during repo map pagerank computation in repomap.py. The error is uncaught and occurs mid-conversation workflow after aider has already started. Platform: Windows 11.

signals.topic: None working_tree_dir causes TypeError crash during GitRepo initialization
signals.summary: When aider is run from a directory that is not inside a Git repository, repo.working_tree_dir returns None, causing a TypeError in pathlib.Path initialization that crashes the app before any workflow begins.
signals.review_reason: Uncaught TypeError crashes the entire application during GitRepo initialization when the working directory is not a git repository. The app gives no graceful error message; users get a raw Python traceback. This is a common user mistake scenario that should be handled with a clear user-facing error message guiding them to initialize a git repo or run from within one.

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in pathlib.py line 373
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: argument should be a str or an os.PathLike object where __fspath__ returns a str, not 'NoneType'. Crash occurs at GitRepo initialization when working_tree_dir is None (not in a git repo). The error is uncaught and prevents any aider usage from non-git directories.

signals.topic: Provider config parameters leak across providers in multi-provider eval, causing API 403 failures
signals.summary: When multiple OpenAI providers are configured in a single eval, provider-level config (e.g., max_tokens) leaks to unrelated providers, causing HTTP 403 errors on newer models that reject max_tokens.
signals.review_reason: This is a high-impact workflow blocker: multi-provider eval fails with HTTP 403 errors due to config isolation bug, forcing users to run separate eval commands as workaround. The failure is reproducible, causes eval to abort entirely, and affects real cost-incurring API calls. Count=1 meets P0 threshold because the user impact (workflow-blocking API failure with no clean in-config workaround) is severe.

source_issues.title: max_tokens config leaks across providers in multi-provider eval
source_issues.evidence: User configures two OpenAI providers in one eval; setting max_tokens on gpt-4.1-mini causes gpt-5.4-mini to fail with HTTP 403 because the leaked parameter is rejected. Workaround requires running separate eval commands with --filter-providers.

signals.topic: openai:agents built-in provider cannot handle multimodal (image) inputs, causing vision eval failures
signals.summary: The openai:agents provider passes prompts as plain strings to the agents SDK, so multimodal content (base64 images) arrives as raw text instead of input_image content blocks, making vision evals fail silently.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core use case of running vision/agent evals with the built-in openai:agents provider. The model receives incorrect input (plain text instead of image content blocks), causing silent eval failures. User must abandon the built-in provider and implement a custom TypeScript workaround that also loses rate limiting/retry logic. High severity because it defeats a first-party integration path entirely.

source_issues.title: openai:agents built-in provider cannot pass multimodal (image) input to the agent
source_issues.evidence: User configures openai:agents provider with a YAML eval containing a base64 image variable; the agent receives raw base64 text instead of a vision content block, model cannot see the image, and evals fail. Workaround requires writing a custom TypeScript function provider that manually builds AgentInputItem[]. Even then, it bypasses built-in rate limiting and retry handling.

signals.topic: apiKeyRequired config not respected for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider, blocking Claude subscription users
signals.summary: Setting apiKeyRequired: false on the anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider does not prevent the provider from requiring an API key, causing Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY errors for users relying on Claude subscriptions instead of API keys.
signals.review_reason: This blocks an entire category of users (Claude subscription-only, no API key) from using the claude-agent-sdk provider at all, despite promptfoo exposing the apiKeyRequired config option. The error is thrown by promptfoo's own logger, confirming the config is not being read or respected. Non-blocking on older models but P1 due to key functionality (subscription-based auth) being completely unavailable.

source_issues.title: apiKeyRequired not working for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
source_issues.evidence: User sets apiKeyRequired: false in promptfoo config for anthropic:claude-agent-sdk and runs without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var (using Claude subscription instead). Promptfoo throws 'Missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' error from its own logger, blocking the eval from running at all.

signals.topic: TypeScript providers fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND when importing other .ts files from the project
signals.summary: TypeScript providers that import other .ts files fail at runtime because promptfoo only transpiles the provider file itself but not its transitive .ts imports, which then go through Node's native module resolution and break.
signals.review_reason: Blocks TypeScript provider users who need to import shared project code to mirror production behavior. Workaround (NODE_OPTIONS='--import tsx') exists but adds a dependency and contradicts the advertised native TypeScript support. Affects users with common project structure patterns. Count=1 and single-repo, so P2 rather than P1, but still a real user pain point with clear workaround burden.

source_issues.title: TypeScript provider fails when importing other .ts files from the project
source_issues.evidence: User creates a TypeScript provider that imports from another .ts file in the project; running promptfoo eval produces ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND error. Workaround requires setting NODE_OPTIONS='--import tsx' and having tsx as a dev dependency, making the 'native TypeScript support' claim misleading.

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses API (GPT-5.x) has multiple round-trip data loss bugs breaking multi-turn tool-calling workflows
signals.summary: Six compounding bugs in llama-index-llms-openai Responses API cause data loss during message round-trip: (1) assistant text silently dropped when tool calls present, (2) phase field not preserved on parsing, (3) phase not serialized back to API, (4) exact model-name lookup for reasoning/sampling params, (5) reasoning token count duplicated across all ThinkingBlocks, (6) tool call arguments not consistently JSON-serialized.
aliases: GPT-5.4 multi-turn tool workflow data loss
tool call arguments not JSON-serialized in Responses API
signals.review_reason: Two issues covering the same component (OpenAI Responses API) with 6 compounding bugs. Issue #21124 has 6 confirmed bugs with full code reproductions — data loss in multi-turn tool workflows is a primary use case for LlamaIndex. The problems include silent text drops, phase parsing failures, and tool call serialization errors that will corrupt agent memory over multi-turn conversations. This is a P0: main flow (multi-turn tool-calling with GPT-5.x) is broken with clear data loss evidence. count=2 provides sufficient basis, and the bugs are explicitly described as production-impacting.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Multiple bugs in llama-index-llms-openai
source_issues.evidence: Six distinct bugs in the OpenAI Responses API with minimal reproductions. Bugs 1-3 compound to break round-trip for GPT-5.4-style multi-turn tool workflows. Bug 4: exact model name lookup causes reasoning options to be silently dropped for dated snapshots like gpt-5.4-2026-03-05. Bug 6: tool call arguments passed as dict cause API errors. 0 comments — likely newly filed.

source_issues.title: [Feature Request]: Responses API version for `OpenAI Like` and `LiteLLM`
source_issues.evidence: Related feature request confirms the Responses API is an active and important integration path. OpenAI is pushing migration from Chat Completions to Responses API, making the underlying bugs in the existing Responses API support a growing user-impact problem.

signals.topic: Ollama streaming drops thinking-only chunks when using extended thinking models (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ)
signals.summary: When streaming from Ollama models that support extended thinking (think=True), chunks where content=None but thinking is present are silently dropped by the stream_chat and astream_chat guard `if r["message"]["content"] is None: continue`. This causes all thinking/reasoning content to be lost during streaming, while the non-streaming chat() works correctly.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed streaming data loss bug in Ollama LLM integration. The root cause is precisely identified (guard condition in stream_chat/astream_chat). Affects all users of extended thinking Ollama models in streaming mode — thinking content is completely absent from streamed output with no error raised, making the issue silent and hard to diagnose. Classified P1 (not P0) because count=1 and single repo, though the user impact is significant.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: stream_chat / astream_chat in llama-index-llms-ollama drops thinking-only chunks
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction steps, identified root cause in base.py lines 474 and 558. Non-streaming chat() correctly handles thinking blocks; streaming path silently drops them. User confirmed with DeepSeek-R1 model, thinking_chunks always empty in streaming mode.

signals.topic: base64 encode returns bytes instead of string causing JSON serialization crashes at runtime
signals.summary: In llama-index-core/img_utils.py, base64.b64encode() returns a bytes object but the function returns it as type str via typing.cast (which only satisfies the type checker, not runtime). Downstream code that concatenates it into strings or serializes to JSON fails with TypeError at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed runtime error causing JSON serialization crashes. The type cast only satisfies the static type checker — at runtime, downstream code that uses the return value in string concatenation or JSON serialization will get TypeError. This is a main flow blocker for any code path that uses base64-encoded images with the OpenAI Responses API or similar. Marked as severity: high by the reporter. Classified P1 (count=1, single repo) but with strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: fix: base64 encode returns bytes instead of string, causing serialization crashes
source_issues.evidence: Bug identified in llama-index-core/llama_index/core/img_utils.py. The function uses typing.cast(str, ...) which does not convert bytes to string at runtime. Downstream code concatenating to f"data:image/jpeg;base64,{img}" or serializing to JSON will fail. Labeled severity: high. 1 comment indicating user discussion.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve blocks the asyncio event loop during query generation, preventing concurrent coroutines from running
signals.summary: In QueryFusionRetriever, _aretrieve calls the synchronous _get_queries() which blocks on self._llm.complete() synchronously. When num_queries > 1 (the default), this blocks the current event loop for the full duration of the LLM HTTP call, preventing other coroutines on the same loop from making progress.
aliases: _aretrieve synchronous LLM call blocks event loop
signals.review_reason: Confirmed async event loop starvation bug in QueryFusionRetriever. The synchronous LLM call inside _aretrieve blocks the event loop, preventing all other coroutines from running until the HTTP call completes. This is a severe async Python anti-pattern that will degrade any application using QueryFusionRetriever in an async context. Classified P1 (count=1, single repo) but with very clear and reproducible user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `QueryFusionRetriever._aretrieve` blocks the event loop during query generation
source_issues.evidence: Bug with full reproduction code showing a coroutine with 0.1s sleep never gets scheduled while retriever._aretrieve is running. Confirmed that other asyncio tasks on the same event loop are starved. Uses default num_queries=4. Root cause: _aretrieve calls synchronous _get_queries() instead of async equivalent.

signals.topic: Google reranker postprocessor fails in production async deployment, causing agents to return 'technical issues' errors
signals.summary: In production (deployed async environment), the Google reranker's _apostprocess_nodes uses RankServiceAsyncClient which causes the React agent to fail and return 'technical issues with the tools I have available' error. The synchronous _postprocess_nodes works correctly; the async implementation is broken in production deployments.
aliases: Google reranker async not working production
Google rerank apostprocess_nodes async production failure
signals.review_reason: Confirmed production failure with high community engagement (7 comments). The Google reranker works in local testing but fails when deployed in a real async production environment, causing the entire agent to return an error message instead of answering. This is a main flow failure for production RAG deployments using Google reranking. The workaround (using asyncio.to_thread) confirms the async implementation is broken. Classified P1 (count=1, single repo) with strong production failure evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Google reranker does not work in production
source_issues.evidence: Bug reported with 7 comments — high community engagement. User reports Google reranker works in Jupyter/tests but fails in deployed React agent. Agent returns 'technical issues with the tools I have available'. Root cause identified: _apostprocess_nodes async path is broken; user workaround is replacing with asyncio.to_thread(self._postprocess_nodes). This is a confirmed production failure blocking the main RAG+rerank workflow.

signals.topic: Daemon crashes: process exits immediately or fails to start on Windows (Node 25 + v3.5.48 upgrade)
signals.summary: The ruflo daemon (claude-flow daemon start) fails to stay alive on Windows with Node.js v25 due to Node 25's unsettled top-level await detection and incorrect Windows spawn options (detached:false). Additionally, v3.5.48 breaks daemon startup because the bundled agentdb package is missing dist/controllers/. The daemon status always shows STOPPED, making the entire background service unusable.
signals.review_reason: Daemon is the core background service of ruflo. Three independent reports from different versions and environments all confirm the daemon fails to stay alive or fails to start, making the entire background intelligence layer unusable. This is a main-flow failure across multiple versions.

source_issues.title: Daemon dies immediately on Windows + Node 25 (unsettled top-level await + detached spawn)
source_issues.evidence: Daemon reports 'started' but exits immediately. daemon status always shows STOPPED. Root cause: Node 25 detects unsettled top-level await (await new Promise(()=>{})) and kills the process when no event loop activity exists. Secondary: detached:false on Windows means child dies when parent exits. 2 comments, detailed root cause analysis with local fix verified.

source_issues.title: ruflo v3.5.48 — daemon crashes: agentdb/dist/controllers/index.js not found
source_issues.evidence: v3.5.48 daemon crashes on startup with error 'Controller index not found: <path>/node_modules/agentdb/dist/controllers/index.js'. Root cause: the bundled agentdb package has only schemas/ and src/ directories, no compiled dist/controllers/. 2 comments, no workaround besides not using daemon.

source_issues.title: AgentDB bridge unavailable — traced to CLI bundling @claude-flow/memory@alpha.11 (missing ControllerRegistry)
source_issues.evidence: All agentdb_* MCP tools return {available: false, error: 'Bridge not available'}. Root cause: @claude-flow/cli bundles @claude-flow/memory@alpha.11 which does not export ControllerRegistry. ESM resolution from npx cache resolves to alpha.11 over project-local alpha.12. 4 comments, detailed tracing with proposed fix.

signals.topic: Trojan detection on bundled agent skills triggers Windows Defender quarantine
signals.summary: Multiple users report that Windows Defender flags and quarantines files in ruflo's bundled agent skills directory (.agents/skills/). Skills containing mining-related content trigger Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB detection. Skills were also triggered hours after install, suggesting passive execution risk.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users experienced real security tool interference. Skills were quarantined before running, blocking use of the feature. The dormant trigger behavior (skills executing hours later) is a concerning pattern. User had to navigate a security incident to use the tool.

source_issues.title: IMPORTANT: Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB Detected
source_issues.evidence: User installed ruflo at 08:48. Windows Defender caught and quarantined files in bundled agent skills before they could run. Skills were triggered hours later after sitting dormant. User explicitly filed this as a security incident.

source_issues.title: Security Vulnerability Report – Trojan:JS/CryoStealz.AE!MTB in .agents/skills/
source_issues.evidence: Separate user filed a formal security vulnerability report about the same trojan detection in .agents/skills/. Report sent to non-existent security email addresses, forcing public disclosure.

signals.topic: Advertised features are stub implementations with no real functionality
signals.summary: Code audit reveals multiple core features are hardcoded stubs: deployment commands return no real output, security scan returns fabricated vulnerability counts, memory quantization reports a hardcoded 3.92x reduction without actual computation, and terminal_execute returns synthetic state-tracking text instead of real command output.
signals.review_reason: Users rely on these features (deployment, security scan, terminal execution) as part of core workflows. When terminal_execute returns fake success without actually running the command, workflows silently break — users believe their automation worked when it didn't. This creates false confidence in production pipelines.

source_issues.title: Security & Reliability Analysis — Independent Review
source_issues.evidence: Code audit found: deployment commands are entirely hardcoded stubs, security scan returns fabricated vulnerability counts, memory quantization reports hardcoded 3.92x reduction factor without actual computation. Features marketed as 'enterprise-grade' appear cosmetic only.

source_issues.title: terminal_execute in MCP does not execute commands; it only returns state-tracking text
source_issues.evidence: terminal_execute always returns '[STATE TRACKING] Command recorded: <command>' with exit code 0 but no actual stdout/stderr. Published build has intentional stub with note 'This is STATE TRACKING only - does not execute commands.' Workflows that depend on command output break or return misleading success.

signals.topic: Init process fragmentation: ruflo init commands create incomplete or non-functional setups
signals.summary: ruflo init --full and ruflo init hooks are two disconnected code paths. init --full creates helper scripts but never registers them in settings.json, so hooks never fire. init hooks creates settings entries but references scripts that don't exist. Users must run both commands manually to get a working setup, and this is not documented.
signals.review_reason: First-run experience is entirely broken. A brand-new user following the documented setup workflow ends up with a non-functional installation where none of the 40+ hooks fire. This blocks the primary use case of the entire tool.

source_issues.title: Bug: init --full and init hooks are disconnected — hooks never fire without manual wiring
source_issues.evidence: init --full creates 40+ helper scripts in .claude/helpers/ but never updates .claude/settings.json with hook entries. README claims hooks 'automatically route tasks' after init, which is false. Both commands must be run manually to get a working setup.

signals.topic: Excessive token consumption: auto-compaction fires frequently and wastes Claude Credits
signals.summary: Since installing ruflo, users experience constant auto-compaction in Claude Code sessions (e.g., 'Compacted Chat - Auto -169K Tokens Freed'). The multiple Skills/MCPs/tools bundled with ruflo are searched and invoked at the beginning of and throughout sessions, burning through tokens even when Claude Code ultimately decides not to use ruflo.
signals.review_reason: Direct, confirmed cost impact: user is paying for Claude API tokens that are being consumed by ruflo's overhead even when ruflo itself is not used. This is a quantifiable financial loss to users on credit-based billing.

source_issues.title: Ruflo causing extreme token usage
source_issues.evidence: User reports constant auto-compaction (169K tokens freed repeatedly) after installing ruflo. Tokens consumed even when Claude Code does not use ruflo tasks, meaning the overhead from scanning all ruflo Skills/MCPs/tools is pure waste. User explicitly states 'using up my Claude Credits extremely fast.' 3 comments with no resolution.

signals.topic: upload command does not accept accessibility tree refs (and cannot handle dynamically created file input elements)
signals.summary: The upload command does not accept accessibility tree refs (e.g. e29) that fill and click commands accept, creating an API inconsistency. Additionally it cannot handle JavaScript-dynamically created <input type="file"> elements, unlike Playwright MCP which detects file chooser dialogs automatically. Users must fall back to CSS selectors for dynamic inputs, and refs from snapshot output cannot be used uniformly.
signals.review_reason: Multiple users blocked from using refs from snapshot output with the upload command — a key workflow for AI agents automating browser tasks. Combined with inability to handle dynamically created file inputs (common in modern web apps), users must fall back to manual CSS selectors, defeating the purpose of accessibility-tree-based automation. Affects agent workflow completeness.

source_issues.title: upload command does not accept accessibility tree refs (fill/click do)
source_issues.evidence: User reported that 'agent-browser upload e29 resume.pdf' fails with 'Element not found' while fill/click work with the same ref format. Identified during a web agent benchmark test against real job application flows.

source_issues.title: agent-browser upload command cannot handle dynamically created file input elements
source_issues.evidence: Upload command cannot locate JavaScript-dynamically created <input type="file"> elements. Playwright MCP can handle the same pattern via dialog detection; agent-browser cannot. Root cause identified as missing dialog detection mechanism.

source_issues.title: bug: agent-browser select fails on custom ARIA combobox widgets
source_issues.evidence: Related: select command also fails on custom ARIA widgets (Radix UI, Headless UI) due to options not being exposed in the AX tree until dropdown opens. Same root mechanism of AX ref handling inconsistency across commands.

signals.topic: --headed flag silently ignored on existing session (no window, no error, no warning)
signals.summary: When a session already has a headless daemon running, passing --headed on subsequent commands produces no window, no error, and no warning. The headed preference is frozen at daemon spawn time and ensure_daemon() returns early for existing sessions.
signals.review_reason: User explicitly passes --headed but the browser remains headless with zero feedback. This causes users to waste time debugging why their browser window does not appear. While not a crash, it is a complete UX failure for headed mode — the user intent is silently discarded with no error or warning. Affects core debugging workflow.

source_issues.title: bug: headed silently ignored on existing session
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer: agent-browser open https://example.com --session test; then agent-browser open https://other.com --headed --session test results in no visible window. Only workaround is closing the session first. Confirmed on v0.16.3, macOS arm64.

source_issues.title: bug: headed silently ignored on existing session
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report from a different author confirming the same behavior on macOS arm64. Root cause identified as ensure_daemon() returning early and AGENT_BROWSER_HEADED being frozen at daemon spawn time.

signals.topic: Browser native confirmation dialogs block agent execution indefinitely
signals.summary: When a browser presents a native confirmation dialog (alert/confirm/prompt), agent-browser does not handle it and the agent waits indefinitely for a response, with no mechanism to dismiss or respond to the dialog.
signals.review_reason: Agent workflow is completely halted by a common browser interaction pattern. Screenshot evidence confirms the dialog is presented and the agent is stuck. This is a main-flow blocker for any automated script encountering confirmation dialogs (e.g., beforeunload, delete confirmations). Count=1 but user impact is severe (complete workflow block with no recovery mechanism).

source_issues.title: Agent Browser can't deal with Browser Native Confirmation Dialogs
source_issues.evidence: Screenshot evidence shows agent blocked waiting on a browser native confirmation dialog. No CDP dialog handling command is exposed to the CLI or agent. Agent workflow is completely halted.

signals.topic: wait --url glob pattern matching broken after Rust rewrite (regression)
signals.summary: The wait --url command does not support glob patterns (*, **) despite documentation and help text showing glob examples. The Rust rewrite replaced Playwright's native glob support with String.includes(), causing all wildcard patterns to never match. This is a regression from v0.15.x.
signals.review_reason: Regression from a working feature: wait --url with glob patterns worked in TypeScript version (v0.15.x) and is now completely broken in Rust rewrite (v0.23.0). Users relying on wait --url '**/settings/profile' patterns will experience indefinite hangs. Breakage of documented behavior with no warning or fallback.

source_issues.title: wait --url glob pattern matching broken after Rust rewrite
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in cli/src/native/actions.rs: wait_for_url uses String.includes() instead of glob matching. Documentation shows glob examples that do not work. Regression from v0.15.x. Also affects route matching and response-body URL matching.

signals.topic: AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS not respected on Unix/macOS (session leak)
signals.summary: The AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable is accepted by the daemon but on Unix/macOS the session remains alive indefinitely instead of shutting down after the configured idle window. Likely cause: idle sleep timer is recreated each loop iteration while the maintenance wake happens every 500ms, preventing the timer from ever reaching its deadline.
signals.review_reason: Resource leak causing daemon processes to remain alive indefinitely on Unix/macOS. Users expecting automatic cleanup (critical for CI environments and cost management) get persistent background processes instead. Clear reproduction with quantified behavior (3s timeout but alive after 31s) and identified root cause in daemon loop logic.

source_issues.title: AGENT_BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS is not respected on Unix/macOS
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows daemon alive after 31 seconds with 3-second timeout configured. Root cause identified in cli/src/native/daemon.rs: idle sleep is recreated each loop iteration while maintenance wakes every 500ms, preventing deadline from being reached.

signals.topic: Malware/Trojan infection during agent-skills package installation causes installation workflow interruption
signals.summary: A user was infected with Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB while installing agent-skills, causing Windows Defender to quarantine files and interrupting the skill installation workflow mid-way.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: the agent-skills package contained malware (Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB) that was delivered through a third-party contribution (ruvnet/ruflo). The user experienced a main workflow interruption (skill installation blocked) and the security software (Windows Defender) had to intervene. This directly impacts users' ability to use the skills and exposes them to credential-stealing malware. Though count=1, the severity is high (credential-stealing trojan) and it is a packaging/supply-chain issue affecting a published package, warranting P1.

source_issues.title: !IMPORTANT: Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB Detected
source_issues.evidence: User reports being interrupted mid-way installing composition-patterns and react-best-practices after ruvnet/ruflo installed 100+ agent-skills containing Trojan:JS/CrypoStealz.AE!MTB, which Windows Defender caught and quarantined before execution.

signals.topic: AI Gateway bills cached tokens at full input price for Moonshot/Kimi — users pay 6x over direct API rates
signals.summary: When using moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 via AI Gateway, cached tokens (93.5% hit rate) are displayed correctly in the dashboard but billed at full input price. A single blog generation session cost ~$4.00 via Gateway vs ~$0.64 direct — 6x overcharge. Root cause may be that Gateway billing doesn't apply cache discounts for implicit-caching providers or multi-backend routing bypasses cache pricing.
aliases: cache discount not applied in AI Gateway for Moonshot
AI Gateway billing ignores cache hits for implicit-caching providers
signals.review_reason: Confirmed billing discrepancy with exact cost math. Dashboard correctly shows 93.5% cache hit rate, yet all input tokens billed at full price — resulting in 6x cost vs direct API. This is direct financial harm to users.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: Cached tokens billed at full input price for Moonshot/Kimi — 6x cost vs direct API
source_issues.evidence: Explicit cost math provided: $4.00 billed vs $1.28 expected. Input 6.2M tokens, 5.8M cache hits, but all billed at full price. Dashboard shows correct cache metrics while billing is wrong.

signals.topic: chat.stop() fires abort signal but returns immediately without waiting for stream pipeline to fully terminate — causes gibberish after clearing chat
signals.summary: When calling chat.stop() (e.g., for a 'clear chat' action), the abort signal fires but stop() returns immediately without waiting for the stream pipeline to fully terminate. Buffered chunks can still arrive after the caller clears messages, resulting in garbled/duplicate output. Users need complex workarounds with manual status callbacks and setTimeout(0) to achieve intuitive behavior.
aliases: chat.stop() race condition with stream termination
stop() returns before stream fully ends
stream chunks arrive after chat clear
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure for any app implementing 'stop' or 'clear chat'. The stream pipeline races with message clearing, causing garbled output. Author explicitly states every app would need the same workaround, indicating widespread impact.

source_issues.title: chat.stop() fires the abort signal but returns immediately without waiting for the stream pipeline to fully terminate
