source_issues.evidence: User provides a full workaround helper showing the problem: stop() fires abort but returns before status changes to 'ready'. The stream's internal job queue can push buffered chunks after the caller clears messages. Comment: 'if we have to wrap it this way then presumably every app that uses ai sdk eventually has to solve the same problems.'

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google drops all custom function tools when provider-defined tools (googleSearch) are present — blocks agents needing both
signals.summary: In @ai-sdk/google's prepareTools, when provider-defined tools (e.g. googleSearch) are present, the function returns early with only those tools — custom function declarations are completely excluded from the API request. This is a hard block for any application that needs Google Search grounding alongside custom function calling. Gemini 3 officially supports combining both, but the SDK silently drops the custom tools with only a warning.
aliases: google provider tools early return drops function declarations
cannot combine googleSearch with custom tools in Gemini 3
function tools silently dropped when provider tools present
signals.review_reason: Key feature of Gemini 3 (tool combination) is blocked. Related issues span multiple years (#8258, #11695, #10251) — this is a known, recurring, unresolved problem that prevents real-world agent use cases. Author provides a verified fix.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google: Support combining provider-defined tools with function tools (Gemini 3 tool combination)
source_issues.evidence: Hard block for agents needing both Google Search grounding and custom function calling. Current behavior: warning 'combination of function and provider-defined tools is not supported', custom tools silently dropped. Verified fix provided. Related issues #11695 (closed without fix), #8258, #10251 (only improved warning message) — this is a recurring unresolved issue.

signals.topic: AI Gateway structured output with Anthropic models intermittently returns 503 on all backends — main workflow failure
signals.summary: When using AI Gateway with streamText + structured output against anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6, requests intermittently fail with GatewayInternalServerError: 'Service temporarily unavailable'. All three Anthropic-family routes (anthropic, vertexAnthropic, bedrock) return 503. Plain-text streamText succeeds 10/10 in the same environment. The failure rate is intermittent, making it a reliability issue for production structured-output workloads.
aliases: AI Gateway 503 on structured output with Anthropic
streamText structured output 503 on anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 via Gateway
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure for structured output via AI Gateway — the same request succeeds as plain text but fails with structured output. Intermittent 503s across all Anthropic backends are a reliability blocker for production deployments using this combination.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway + streamText structured output intermittently returns 503 for Anthropic model while plain text succeeds
source_issues.evidence: Intermittent GatewayInternalServerError with 503 on all three Anthropic routes. Plain-text repro succeeds 10/10. Structured output fails with service_unavailable_error. Multiple request IDs provided. Author notes: 'should not intermittently fail on such a small schema if the plain-text path is healthy.'

signals.topic: MCP OAuth resource URL trailing slash causes token exchange to fail on servers using exact URI matching
signals.summary: When the MCP server returns a pathless resource URL (e.g., https://mcp.example.com), new URL().href appends a trailing slash per URL spec. Auth servers using exact URI matching reject the token exchange because the trailing slash makes it a different URI. The MCP spec itself recommends the form without trailing slash for interoperability. Affects startAuthorization, exchangeAuthorization, and refreshAuthorization.
aliases: MCP OAuth trailing slash in resource parameter
OAuth resource URL.href appends trailing slash breaking exact-match auth servers
signals.review_reason: MCP OAuth flow is completely broken for auth servers doing exact URI matching. The MCP spec explicitly recommends the form without trailing slash, yet SDK adds it. This is a blocker for MCP server authentication in enterprise environments.

source_issues.title: OAuth resource parameter gets trailing slash from URL.href, breaking auth servers that do exact matching
source_issues.evidence: OAuth token exchange fails because resource parameter is sent as https://mcp.example.com/ instead of https://mcp.example.com. MCP spec explicitly recommends form without trailing slash for interoperability. Related modelcontextprotocol/inspector#927 confirms cross-repo impact.

signals.topic: Turbopack crashes on exponentiation (**) operator due to SWC compatibility transforms bug

signals.review_reason: Two distinct issues causing Turbopack to crash (panic) on the ** operator, a common JavaScript feature. Both block the primary development and build workflow — users cannot compile their projects. This is a main flow blocker for any developer using Turbopack with styled-components or projects that trigger SWC compat transforms.

signals.topic: ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT and hydration mismatch when using 'use cache' directive with draftMode() or cookies() in the same component
signals.summary: Using the experimental 'use cache' directive together with draftMode() or cookies() in the same page component causes ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT error and __next_metadata_boundary__ hydration mismatch, breaking page rendering entirely.
aliases: use cache directive conflict with draftMode
signals.review_reason: Two issues describing a runtime error when combining the experimental 'use cache' directive with draft mode or cookies — two commonly-used Next.js features. ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT and hydration mismatch produce broken pages with cryptic errors. While count=2, this is a newer experimental feature (not yet default), so classified P1 rather than P0.

CORS is a web standard — this breaks any cross-origin setup. Labeled P1 (not P0) because one of the two issues is marked 'invalid link', reducing confidence that it's broadly affecting users.

signals.topic: generateBuildId in next.config.ts is ignored and replaced with auto-generated ID in v16.2.0+, breaking cache invalidation
signals.summary: Custom generateBuildId function configured in next.config.ts is not respected after upgrading to v16.2.0+. The build process ignores the custom build ID and uses an auto-generated one instead, breaking cache invalidation strategies that rely on deterministic build IDs.
signals.review_reason: User has a full reproduction repo showing generateBuildId is ignored in v16.2.0+. This breaks cache invalidation strategies that rely on deterministic build IDs — a core feature for incremental static regeneration and Vercel deployment workflows. Clear regression from v16.1.x.

source_issues.title: `generateBuildId` in `next.config.ts` not respected in v16.2.0+
source_issues.evidence: Custom generateBuildId function is ignored in v16.2.0+ and replaced with auto-generated ID. User provided a full reproduction repo. Breaks cache invalidation strategies that depend on deterministic build IDs.

signals.topic: createProject API breaking change: secret environment variable type removed without documentation warning
signals.summary: The createProject method in vercel.projects no longer accepts the 'secret' type for environment variables, breaking existing code with no deprecation notice or documentation update.
signals.review_reason: This is a breaking API change that blocks users from creating projects with secret environment variables using the SDK. The user explicitly states their production is broken and there is no documentation warning about the removed 'secret' type. This constitutes a main workflow failure with clear user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: [BREAKING CHANGE|DOC ISSUE]: vercel.projects.createProject no longer support secret vars so it breaks current code
source_issues.evidence: User reports that createProject no longer accepts the 'secret' type for environment variable creation, breaking their production workflow. The documentation and package types provide no warning about this removed option. The issue is open and recently active.

signals.topic: `turbo prune --docker` generates inconsistent lockfiles causing `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `npm ci` to fail in Docker builds
signals.summary: `turbo prune --docker` produces a pruned lockfile that retains top-level entries from removed workspaces while the surviving subgraph still references older versions. This breaks both `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen) and `npm ci` (missing modules after prune). Users cannot containerize their builds.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：prune 是 monorepo Docker 构建流程的核心步骤，生成的 lockfile 与实际依赖图不一致导致所有容器化构建直接失败。两条独立 issue 均证实跨多种包管理器（npm/bun）均可复现。

source_issues.title: `turbo prune --docker` keeps removed-workspace versions as top-level Bun entries, breaking `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
source_issues.evidence: Pruned bun.lock keeps newer top-level entries from removed frontend workspace while backend graph still references older package versions. bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts fails with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'. Multiple package managers affected.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune`: cannot install packages after pruning when using npm shallow install strategy
source_issues.evidence: After npx turbo prune and npm ci in pruned repo, npm cannot find all required modules. serverless/scripts/postinstall.js cannot find module 'chalk'. Generated package-lock.json not using shallow install strategy, causing serverless at root while chalk ends up in wrong folder.

signals.topic: `turbo prune` npm shallow install strategy generates inconsistent package-lock.json causing missing modules after prune
signals.summary: After `npx turbo prune @foobar/analytics-endpoint --docker --out-dir=/tmp/foobar-pruned` and then `npm ci` in the pruned repo, npm cannot find all required modules. The generated package-lock.json is not using the shallow install strategy, causing serverless package at root while chalk ends up in analytics-util folder. Module resolution fails.
aliases: turbo prune missing modules npm ci
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：prune 是 Docker 容器化构建的基础设施，生成的 package-lock.json 结构错误导致 npm ci 直接失败，用户无法完成容器镜像构建。两条独立 issue 均提供具体复现步骤，影响确定。

source_issues.title: `turbo prune`: cannot install packages after pruning when using npm shallow install strategy
source_issues.evidence: npm ci in pruned repo fails: serverless/scripts/postinstall.js cannot find module chalk. package-lock.json not using shallow install strategy causes serverless at root while chalk in analytics-util folder.

source_issues.title: Cache is extracted to wrong destination

signals.topic: `turbo watch` cascading task restarts corrupt TUI and cause exponential rebuilds in deep dependency graphs
signals.summary: When running `turbo watch` in monorepos with multi-layer dependencies, file changes trigger cascading restarts: a build task completing writes `dist/` output which `turbo watch` detects as another file change, restarting all dependents. This creates exponential redundant restarts and on Windows ConPTY makes TUI completely unreadable. `turbo run dev` does not have this problem.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：持续文件监听循环导致 watch 模式在生产级 monorepo 中完全不可用，开发者无法正常进行增量开发循环。TUI 渲染崩溃进一步加重体验劣化。

source_issues.title: `turbo watch` triggers cascading task restarts in deep dependency graphs, garbling TUI
source_issues.evidence: Build completing writes dist/ output, turbo watch detects it as file change, restarts all dependents. 30-package monorepo with 3-4 layers causes dozens of redundant restarts. Windows ConPTY TUI completely unreadable. turbo run dev does NOT have this problem.

signals.topic: `turbo watch` crashes in Devcontainers/Codespaces due to Rust-level reference counting panic with bind mounts
signals.summary: When running `turbo watch` inside a Devcontainers setup in GitHub Codespaces with a bind mount via docker compose, turbo crashes with a panic at `crates/turborepo-lib/src/task_graph/visitor/mod.rs:564` with error 'only one strong reference to errors should remain'. `turbo run` works fine, only `turbo watch` is affected. Full stack trace and TOML crash report provided.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：云开发环境（Codespaces）下 watch 模式直接崩溃，Rust 层面的引用计数 panic，开发者无法在主流云开发环境中使用 turborepo 进行日常开发。

source_issues.title: Turbo watch crashes with a bind mount in a Devcontainers setup in GitHub Codespaces
source_issues.evidence: Crash at crates/turborepo-lib/src/task_graph/visitor/mod.rs:564 with error 'only one strong reference to errors should remain'. turbo run works perfectly, only turbo watch crashes. Reproducible in GitHub Codespaces with docker compose bind mount.

signals.topic: Cache artifacts extracted to wrong destination after first build, causing build files to land in `src/` instead of `dist/`
signals.summary: When executing a build for the first time everything generates and caches correctly. On subsequent runs the cache is restored to the wrong directory — build files end up in `src/` instead of `dist/`. The issue occurs with a package that has both a build task and a dev:prepare task depending on it, both declaring `dist/` as output. Minimal reproduction repo provided.
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：缓存命中后产物写入错误目录，导致构建产物污染源码目录。在 CI 环境中缓存回填错误路径会引发后续构建行为异常，具有隐蔽性难以快速定位。

source_issues.title: Cache is extracted to wrong destination
source_issues.evidence: First build: everything generates correctly and is cached. Second run: existing cache restored to wrong directory, build files end up in src/ instead of dist/. Package has build task depending on dev:prepare task, both with dist/ as output.

signals.topic: CLI env subcommands block CI/CD automation (stdin redirect fails and --yes/--force flags ignored)
signals.summary: Two related bugs in `vercel env` CLI subcommands make it impossible to automate environment variable management in CI/CD pipelines: (1) `vercel env update <name> < file` errors with 'Invalid number of arguments' despite matching documented usage and `--value` behavior; (2) `vercel env add <name> preview --value <val> --yes --force` still prompts for git branch interactively, hanging in GitHub Actions and similar non-interactive environments.
aliases: vercel env add preview ignores --yes --force flags
vercel env update stdin redirect broken
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed CLI bugs that directly block CI/CD automation for environment variable management. Issue 15763 hangs GitHub Actions workflows (non-interactive CI blocking). Issue 15764 breaks stdin-based input in automation pipelines. Both are regressions from documented/expected behavior. Count=2 meets frequency threshold with sample links.

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env update <name> < file` fails without target, but `--value` works
source_issues.evidence: CLI errors with 'Invalid number of arguments' when using stdin redirect without target, but --value flag works for the same operation. Breaks automation pipelines relying on file-based input.

source_issues.evidence: CLI prompts interactively for git branch in CI/CD environments (GitHub Actions) despite --yes, --force, --non-interactive flags. Forces users to fall back to REST API as workaround, directly blocking CI/CD automation.

signals.topic: CLI deployment of Turborepo monorepo with internal workspace packages fails on Vercel servers
signals.summary: Deploying a single app from a Turborepo monorepo via `vercel --prod` fails because Vercel only uploads files within the app directory and does not resolve internal workspace packages (e.g., `@xolito/marketing` depends on `@xolito/tailwind`). All attempted workarounds (custom installCommand, workspace flags) fail due to Vercel's concurrent npm install interfering.
aliases: Turborepo monorepo CLI deployment internal packages
vercel CLI monorepo internal package resolution fails
signals.review_reason: Core deployment workflow blocked. Deploying a monorepo app via CLI is a fundamental use case that fails with a clear build error (404 for internal packages). The user attempted all standard workarounds without success. Though count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence: primary deployment path fails completely.

source_issues.title: CLI deployment of turbo monorepo with internal packages fails
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with 'npm error 404 Not Found' for internal workspace packages when deploying via CLI (not Git integration). Multiple workarounds attempted and all failed. Blocks the core use case of deploying monorepo apps via CLI, which is a primary deployment path for many developers.

signals.topic: vercel.json configuration loses efficacy during CLI-triggered builds since CLI v50.1.3
signals.summary: Deploying via `npx vercel ./out/xxxx/ --prod --archive=tgz` no longer respects vercel.json settings since CLI version 50.1.3. Previous deployments with CLI 50.0.0 and 49.1.2 worked correctly. The configuration appears to be ignored during the server-side build step.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression that breaks vercel.json functionality for CLI-triggered builds. Though count=1, the user provided clear before/after build logs showing the regression. However, P2 is assigned because the issue is older (Dec 2025) and was closed, suggesting it may have been addressed or is less actively impacting users compared to the two P0 issues.

source_issues.title: vercel.json lost efficacy since 50.1.3 while build locally
source_issues.evidence: Regression introduced in CLI 50.1.3: vercel.json configuration is ignored during CLI-triggered builds. Build logs show 'Skipping cache upload because no files were prepared' and build completes differently than with prior CLI versions. The issue was closed but reopened/active with user confirmation of ongoing impact.

signals.topic: Helix mode crashes when using match command with multiple selections
signals.summary: Users experience a hard crash of Zed when pressing the match command (m) in helix mode after making multiple selections using visual mode with next-match (n). This is a complete editor crash with no partial workaround.
aliases: crash on v n n n then m
signals.review_reason: Hard crash that fully blocks the editor during a normal helix-mode editing workflow. Reproducible via exact key sequence. Count=1 but crash severity and workflow blockage warrant P0.

source_issues.title: Crash on match with multiple selections in helix mode
source_issues.evidence: User reports crash when pressing 'm' (match) after 'v n n n' (visual + next match) in helix mode. No log captured. OS: Linux Wayland Manjaro. GPU: AMD RX 6900 XT.

signals.topic: Remote SSH extensions fail to install when TMPDIR is on a different mount than HOME
signals.summary: When using Zed over SSH with remote, if the server's TMPDIR is on a separate volume from HOME, extension installation fails silently due to a cross-mount fs.rename error. Language servers then fail to spawn, breaking the core remote development experience.
aliases: R language server fails on remote SSH
signals.review_reason: Remote SSH development is a core use case. Extension installation failure prevents ALL language servers from running on remote, which is a complete remote-development blockage. Error log confirms fs.rename cross-mount failure.

source_issues.title: Remote SSH extensions installs fail when TMPDIR is on different mount than HOME
source_issues.evidence: Error log shows: 'Failed to rename {tmp_path:?} to {path:?}: Invalid argument (os error 22)'. R language server does not spawn. This broke after v0.227.1. All remote extensions affected.

signals.topic: ACP external agent hangs waiting for permission approval with no UI buttons displayed
signals.summary: When an ACP external agent (e.g., kilo-cli) attempts to use a tool requiring user permission, Zed shows a permission dialog box but without any Allow/Deny buttons. The agent hangs indefinitely waiting for a response that cannot be given, completely stalling the AI agent workflow.
aliases: ACP agent hangs on tool permission dialog
kilo-cli agent stuck waiting for approval
tool permission approval dialog missing buttons
signals.review_reason: Agent workflow is completely blocked with no possible user action to unblock. The permission UI is broken — dialog appears but has no interactive buttons, and the agent logs incorrectly claim user rejection. This defeats the entire ACP external agent integration.

source_issues.title: ACP integration with kilo-cli hangs expecting user approval but UI does not reflect that
source_issues.evidence: Agent log shows: 'Error: The user rejected permission to use this specific tool call.' User confirms they did NOT reject. Permission dialog shows with title 'Run command' but no confirmation buttons. Agent stuck waiting. Reproduced with multiple models (Claude Sonnet 4.6, Minimax M2.5).

signals.topic: Debugger rerun session does not execute the build task before restarting
signals.summary: When a user clicks 'Rerun Session' in the debugger, Zed restarts the debug session but skips the configured build task that was run on the initial launch. This breaks the standard debug iteration loop where developers modify code and restart.
aliases: debugger rerun not running build command
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core debug iteration workflow (modify -> build -> run -> repeat). Count=1 but user explicitly states this makes the debugger 'barely usable' and a prior PR claimed to fix this but the regression exists. Non-blocking but significant workflow degradation.

source_issues.title: Debugger: Rerun Session does not run the build task
source_issues.evidence: User has debug.json with a build command. First run executes build correctly. Clicking 'rerun session' restarts without running the build. User notes: 'the debugger is already a janky experience compared to VSCode... issues like this make it barely usable.'

signals.topic: LSP edit application silently corrupts source code with overlapping/nested edits on save
signals.summary: When an LSP returns overlapping or nested edits (e.g., from source.fixAll.oxc sort-keys on nested JavaScript objects), Zed's edit-merging logic produces malformed replacement strings that corrupt the source file, deleting and garbling code beyond recovery from the buffer state.
aliases: oxc formatter corrupts file on save
nested sort-keys fix corrupts JS file
LSP TextEdit merge produces malformed string
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption of user source code is a severe issue. The corruption happens during the save operation and is not recoverable without external version control. Impact is high even at count=1. Well-documented with clear reproduction and log evidence.

source_issues.title: source.fixAll.oxc on save corrupts nested sort-keys fixes
source_issues.evidence: User provides before/after code showing file content is permanently corrupted (deleted lines, garbled object keys). Zed log shows the malformed string is already wrong before buffer.edit() is called. Same repo and oxc fix works in VS Code. Root cause traced to edit-merging in lsp_store.rs.
